126	    out = []
127	    for fn in sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(SRC, "class"))):
128	        if not fn.startswith("class-") or not fn.endswith(".json"): continue
129	        data = load("class", fn)
130	        for c in data.get("class", []):
131	            if not is_phb(c): continue
132	            sp = c.get("startingProficiencies", {})
133	            sk_fixed, sk_choose = skills_from(sp.get("skills"))
134	            seen, subs = set(), []
135	            for s in data.get("subclass", []):
136	                if not is_phb(s) or s.get("className") != c["name"]: continue
137	                short = s.get("shortName", s["name"])
138	                if short in seen: continue
139	                seen.add(short); subs.append({"name": s["name"], "short": short})
140	            out.append({"name": c["name"],
141	                        "hd": c.get("hd", {}).get("faces"),
142	                        "saves": c.get("proficiency", []),
143	                        "skillChoose": sk_choose, "skillsFixed": sk_fixed,
144	                        "armor": render_prof_list(sp.get("armor")), "weapons": render_prof_list(sp.get("weapons")),
145	                        "casterAbility": c.get("spellcastingAbility"),
146	                        "casterProgression": c.get("casterProgression"),
147	                        "subclassTitle": c.get("subclassTitle",""), "subclasses": subs})
148	    return out
149	
150	def build_feats(raw):
151	    out = []
152	    for f in raw.get("feat", []):
153	        if not is_phb(f): continue
154	        out.append({"name": f["name"], "text": entries_to_text(f.get("entries", []))})
155	    return out
156	
157	def build_items(raw):
158	    weapons, armor = [], []
159	    for it in raw.get("baseitem", []):
160	        if not is_phb(it): continue
161	        if it.get("weapon"):
162	            weapons.append({"name": it["name"], "cat": "martial" if it.get("weaponCategory")=="martial" else "simple",
163	                            "dmg": it.get("dmg1",""), "dmgType": DMG.get(it.get("dmgType",""), it.get("dmgType","")),
164	                            "versatile": it.get("dmg2",""),
165	                            "props": [WPROP.get(p, p) for p in (it.get("property") or [])],
166	                            "range": it.get("range","")})
167	        elif it.get("armor") or it.get("type","") in ("LA","MA","HA","S"):
168	            armor.append({"name": it["name"], "ac": it.get("ac"), "type": it.get("type",""),
169	                          "stealth": bool(it.get("stealth")), "strength": it.get("strength")})
170	    return weapons, armor
171	
172	def build_spells():
173	    spells = []
174	    for fn in os.listdir(os.path.join(SRC, "spells")):
175	        if not re.match(r"spells-phb\.json$", fn): continue
176	        for s in load("spells", fn).get("spell", []):
177	            if not is_phb(s): continue
178	            comp = s.get("components", {})
179	            spells.append({"name": s["name"], "level": s.get("level", 0),
180	                           "school": SCHOOL.get(s.get("school",""), s.get("school","")),
181	                           "time": entries_to_text(s.get("time", [])) if isinstance(s.get("time"), str) else
182	                                   "; ".join(f"{t.get('number','')} {t.get('unit','')}" for t in s.get("time", [])),
183	                           "range": render_range(s.get("range", {})),
184	                           "components": "".join(k.upper() for k in ("v","s","m") if comp.get(k)),
185	                           "duration": render_duration(s.get("duration", [])),
186	                           "text": entries_to_text(s.get("entries", [])),
187	                           "higher": entries_to_text(s.get("entriesHigherLevel", []))})
188	    spells.sort(key=lambda x: (x["level"], x["name"]))
189	    return spells
190	
191	# Items that grant a flat AC bonus (shield, rings/cloaks/bracers of protection, etc.) for the
192	# Armor section's bonus-item pickers. PHB only has the Shield, so this pulls from the wider data.
193	def build_ac_items():
194	    out, seen = [{"n": "Shield", "b": 2}], {"Shield"}
195	    try: items = load("items.json").get("item", [])
196	    except Exception: return out
197	    for it in items:
198	        b = it.get("bonusAc")
199	        if not b: continue
200	        if (it.get("type") or "").split("|")[0] in ("LA", "MA", "HA"): continue   # body armor → Armor dropdown
201	        name = it.get("name", "")
202	        if name in seen: continue
203	        try: bonus = int(str(b).replace("+", "").strip())
204	        except Exception: continue
205	        seen.add(name); out.append({"n": name, "b": bonus})
206	    out.sort(key=lambda x: x["n"])
207	    return out
208	
209	# Per-class PHB spell lists (levels 1-9) for classes that prepare from their whole list.
210	def build_class_spells():
211	    levels = {}
212	    for fn in os.listdir(os.path.join(SRC, "spells")):
213	        if not re.match(r"spells-phb\.json$", fn): continue
214	        for s in load("spells", fn).get("spell", []):
215	            if is_phb(s): levels[s["name"]] = s.get("level", 0)
216	    try: src = load("spells", "sources.json").get("PHB", {})
217	    except Exception: return {}
218	    FULL = {"Cleric", "Druid", "Paladin", "Artificer"}
219	    out = {}
220	    for name, info in src.items():
221	        lv = levels.get(name)
222	        if lv is None or lv == 0: continue            # PHB, leveled spells only (cantrips go in their own box)
223	        for c in info.get("class", []):
224	            if c.get("source") == PHB and c.get("name") in FULL:
225	                out.setdefault(c["name"], []).append({"n": name, "l": lv})
226	    for cn in out: out[cn].sort(key=lambda x: (x["l"], x["n"]))
227	    return out
228	
229	def render_range(r):
230	    if not isinstance(r, dict): return str(r)
231	    d = r.get("distance", {})
232	    if r.get("type") == "point" and d: return f"{d.get('amount','')} {d.get('type','')}".strip()
233	    return r.get("type", "")
234	
235	def render_duration(d):
236	    if not d: return ""
237	    x = d[0]
238	    if x.get("type") == "timed":
239	        dur = x.get("duration", {})
240	        return f"{'Concentration, up to ' if x.get('concentration') else ''}{dur.get('amount','')} {dur.get('type','')}"
241	    return x.get("type", "")
242	
243	def main():
244	    races = load("races.json")
245	    out = {
246	        "_meta": {"book": "Player's Handbook (2014)",
247	                  "source": "D&D 5e PHB (2014) via local 5eTools — personal use, do not redistribute"},
248	        "races": build_races(races),
249	        "backgrounds": build_backgrounds(load("backgrounds.json")),
250	        "classes": build_classes(),
251	        "feats": build_feats(load("feats.json")),
252	        "spells": build_spells(),
253	        "classSpells": build_class_spells(),
254	        "acItems": build_ac_items(),
255	    }
256	    weapons, armor = build_items(load("items-base.json"))
257	    out["weapons"], out["armor"] = weapons, armor
258	    json.dump(out, open(OUT, "w"), separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
259	    sz = os.path.getsize(OUT)
260	    print(f"wrote {OUT}  ({sz/1024:.0f} KB)")
261	    for k, v in out.items():
262	        if isinstance(v, list): print(f"  {k}: {len(v)}")
263	    build_sheet(out)
264	    return out
265	
266	def build_sheet(data):
267	    """Bake the PHB data into a personal single-file copy of the sheet (gitignored)."""
268	    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
269	    app = os.path.join(here, "Character Sheet.html")
270	    out = os.path.join(here, "Character Sheet (PHB).html")
271	    if not os.path.exists(app):
272	        print("  (skip build_sheet: Character Sheet.html not found)"); return
273	    html = open(app).read()
274	    blob = json.dumps(data, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
275	    new = re.sub(r'(<script id="phb-data" type="application/json">).*?(</script>)',
276	                 lambda m: m.group(1) + blob + m.group(2), html, count=1, flags=re.S)
277	    if new == html:
278	        print("  (skip build_sheet: no #phb-data block in Character Sheet.html yet)"); return
279	    open(out, "w").write(new)
280	    print(f"  baked -> {out}  ({os.path.getsize(out)/1024:.0f} KB)")
281	
282	if __name__ == "__main__":
283	    main()

- **Settings** → page-layout toggles (hide/show any tab) and **Source books** (see below).

  and portrait in place). The loaded sourcebook is kept.

## Source books (Settings)
Open **Settings → Source books** to load D&D content. Two ways:
- **From a local 5etools server** — pick any book (PHB, XGE, TCE, …) and click **Load**. The sheet
  fetches the raw 5etools JSON from your server (default `http://localhost:5050`, editable) and
  processes it **in the browser** (a JS port of `build-data.py`). Loading more books **merges** them
  (dedup by name), so you can stack sources. Works fully offline as long as that local server is
  running — nothing is fetched from the internet.
- **Import file…** — load a pre-built `phb-data.json` (made by `build-data.py`) when you don't want
  to run a server.
Loaded data is remembered per browser (localStorage). It is **copyrighted WotC content for personal
use** — it lives only in your browser and is never committed; the shipped app stays content-free.

Done. You can now load any 5etools sourcebook directly from your local server, in the browser, with offline support.

**How it works (Settings → Source books):**
- A **book picker** populated from your server's `books.json` (all 60 books — PHB, XGE, TCE, etc.) plus a **Load** button.
- An editable **5etools server** field (defaults to `http://localhost:5050`, remembered between sessions).
- Clicking **Load** fetches the raw 5etools JSON from your server and processes it **entirely in the browser** — I ported `build-data.py`'s whole extraction pipeline (tag-stripping, races/subraces, classes, backgrounds, feats, spells with all properties, class spell lists, weapons/armor, AC items) into JavaScript.

text: Just to clarify, when I "load" source books, do they then live in the HTML file afterwards?

blocks.text: Good question — let me be precise, since the answer differs by mechanism.

blocks.name: Bash

input.command: cd "/Users/alexhedtke/Documents/dnd-character-sheet" && grep -n 'btn-savecopy' "Character Sheet.html"; sed -n '/btn-savecopy").addEventListener/,/});/p' "Character Sheet.html"

blocks.text:
No — by default, loading a sourcebook does **not** write it into the HTML file. Here's exactly where the data lives:

**When you click "Load":**
- The book is fetched from your local 5etools server, processed in memory, and saved to that **browser's `localStorage`** (key `dnd-sheet-sources`).
- The `.html` file on disk is **never modified**.

**What that means:**
- ✅ It **persists across reloads/restarts** in that same browser, and is shared across tabs/slots opened from the same location.
- ❌ It does **not** travel if you copy/move/AirDrop the `.html` file — a fresh browser opening that file starts without it.
- ❌ It is **not** included in a **Save** copy. Save only bakes your *character* (and portrait) into the file's `#embedded-data`; it leaves the sourcebook block alone.
- 🧹 Clearing the browser's site data wipes it (you'd just re-Load). **Reset** does *not* wipe it (Reset only clears the character).

**The one exception:** the `(PHB)` build itself has PHB baked into the file's `#phb-data` block — but that was done by `build-data.py` at build time, not by the in-app loader. Anything you Load on top of it lives only in localStorage.

So the model is: **PHB is baked into the file; books you Load are an in-browser overlay.**

If you'd rather loaded books **bake into the file** (so a Saved copy or a moved file carries them), I can add that — e.g., make "Save" also write the merged sourcebook into `#phb-data`, or add a "Bake sourcebooks into this file" action. That copy would contain copyrighted data, so it'd stay a personal/gitignored file (like the current `(PHB)` build), never committed. Want me to add it?

    out, bases, base_idx = [], {}, {}
    for r in raw.get("race", []):
        if not is_phb(r): continue
        ab = list(r.get("ability") or [])
        bases[r["name"]] = {"ability": ab, "speed": _speed(r), "traits": _traits(r.get("entries", []))}
        base_idx[r["name"]] = len(out)
        out.append({"name": r["name"], "ability": ab,

    for s in raw.get("subrace", []):
        if not is_phb(s): continue
        parent = s.get("raceName")
        if not s.get("name"):                       # unnamed "standard" subrace -> fold into base option
            i = base_idx.get(parent)
            if i is not None:

        out.append({"name": f"{parent} ({s['name']})",

def race_langs(r):
    out = []
    for blk in r.get("languageProficiencies") or []:
        for k, v in blk.items():
            if v is True: out.append(k[:1].upper() + k[1:])
            elif isinstance(v, int) and v:
                kind = {"anyStandard": " (standard)", "anyExotic": " (exotic)", "any": ""}.get(k, " (" + k + ")")
                out.append(f"{v} language{'s' if v > 1 else ''} of your choice{kind}")
    return out

def build_races(raw):
    out, bases, base_idx = [], {}, {}
    for r in raw.get("race", []):
        if not is_phb(r): continue
        ab = list(r.get("ability") or [])
        bases[r["name"]] = {"ability": ab, "speed": _speed(r), "traits": _traits(r.get("entries", [])), "langs": race_langs(r)}
        base_idx[r["name"]] = len(out)
        out.append({"name": r["name"], "ability": ab,
                    "size": "/".join(SIZE.get(s, s) for s in r.get("size", [])) or "Medium",
                    "speed": _speed(r), "traits": _traits(r.get("entries", [])), "langs": race_langs(r)})
    for s in raw.get("subrace", []):
        if not is_phb(s): continue
        parent = s.get("raceName")
        if not s.get("name"):                       # unnamed "standard" subrace -> fold into base option
            i = base_idx.get(parent)
            if i is not None:
                out[i]["ability"] = (out[i]["ability"] or []) + (s.get("ability") or [])
                out[i]["traits"]  = (out[i]["traits"] or []) + _traits(s.get("entries", []))
                out[i]["langs"]   = (out[i].get("langs") or []) + race_langs(s)
            continue
        base = bases.get(parent, {})               # named subrace -> "Race (Subrace)", base + subrace
        out.append({"name": f"{parent} ({s['name']})",
                    "ability": (base.get("ability") or []) + (s.get("ability") or []),
                    "size": "", "speed": _speed(s) if s.get("speed") is not None else base.get("speed", 30),
                    "subraceOf": parent,
                    "traits": (base.get("traits") or []) + _traits(s.get("entries", [])),
                    "langs": (base.get("langs") or []) + race_langs(s)})
    return out

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: The overarching project is a single self-contained, offline, no-Adobe D&D 5e (2014 rules) character sheet as one HTML file (`Character Sheet.html`), with copyrighted PHB/5etools content kept strictly out of the public repo. This conversation segment was a long series of incremental refinements. In chronological order the explicit requests were: - Add a dedicated "Hit Dice" section (what dice / used / available), moved out of Combat; later "Total" = quantity and the Hit Dice box should read "1d8+3" (one die + Con mod). - Remove the "5d8" placeholder. - Add a "Senses" box under Skills holding Passive Perception + a free-form field that auto-fills darkvision etc. from race; keep it on page 1; make Passive Perception prominent, then same size as skill boxes, then one line. - Re-tool the Abilities box: sheet shows only Score + Modifier; an "Under the hood" button (hidden in print) opens a modal with generation method + ASI/Racial/Magical/Misc bonus columns + notes. Label the Score/Modifier columns ("Mod" to avoid clipping). - Tighten/standardize Combat boxes; turn Death Saves em-dash into a colon, then bold "Death Saves:" and shift Successes/Failures right; remove Speed placeholder; standardize Initiative font; remove the misc-initiative box. - Page 2: enlarge Carrying Capacity boxes (writable), add 3 Attuned Items, make Inventory fill remaining space; rename "Equipment and Notes" → "Equipment Notes" and reorder (Currency, Attuned, Inventory, Equipment Notes, Carrying Capacity). - Page 3 Features & Traits fills the whole page; Page 4 add Allies/Enemies; Page 5 = single Backstory box filling page (delete Allies & Organizations + Additional Notes); add a "Notes" tab (full-page text), placed after Spells. - Spell page (page 6) overhaul: slots show Total + Expended; cantrips listed like other spells (no Lvl/Prep), 5 entries; sections per level with 10 entries each; spill across pages; sections expand/shrink per character generation; add per-spell Components(V/S/M)/Cast Time/Range/Duration/School + hover description; class+level filter the visible spell levels in BOTH list and slots; "Can Prepare" stat for prepared casters; taller DC/Attack/Can-Prepare boxes; remove redundant per-row Lvl column. - Settings button with a "Layout" section to hide/show any tab (remove the redundant spell-sheet include checkbox); add a "Source books" section and move the Import button into it; name the loaded sourcebook ("Player's Handbook (2014)"). - Load sourcebooks in-browser from the user's LOCAL 5etools server (no internet), for any book; bake loaded books into the data file via download; rename outputs off "PHB" to "source data." - Numerous bug fixes: AC not auto-calculating; Monk shows no starting equipment; Artificer auto-getting Tasha's Caustic Brew; class features not added; Thieves' Tools missing; Wood Elf speed 30 not 35. - Character creation enhancements: prompt for class skill choices; prompt starting gold vs equipment with weapon-category and pack-contents sub-prompts; resolve picks into Inventory; "Custom Background" walkthrough (skills, tools/languages dropdowns, feature picker); race languages → Proficiencies box; subclass hidden until level qualifies. - Combat rules automation: Monk/Barbarian Unarmored Defense AC; encumbrance reduces movement (variant rule, with disadvantage note); Monk Unarmored Movement adds to speed; all movement modifications replace the base speed shown in the single page-1 Speed box. - Inventory: auto-calculate item weights; deleting an item clears its qty/weight; drag items to reorder; 2 columns; left-justified; wider qty/wt boxes; taller print rows; +8 then +6 rows (now 34 total). - Make Combat HP boxes same size as AC/Init/Speed. - Make the Features & Traits box auto-expand on screen to show full content (the last feature). - Final: "Commit and push." 2. Key Technical Concepts: - Single self-contained HTML file: vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no frameworks/CDN/web-fonts, fully offline; localStorage persistence (KEY, SOURCES_KEY="dnd-sheet-sources", SERVER_KEY="dnd-sheet-5et-server", per-tab #slot=). - In-browser port of `build-data.py` (the `et*` functions: etTags, etText, etRaces, etRaceLangs, etBackgrounds, etClasses, etFeats, etSpells, etClassSpells, etItems, etAcItems, etLanguages, etTools, etPacks, etItemWeights) to fetch/process raw 5etools JSON from a local server (localhost:5050, CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`). - `DATA_VERSION` gate (currently 9) in `_meta.dataVersion`; init prefers stored SOURCES_KEY only if `srcComplete()` AND same version as baked, else uses baked — prevents stale stored data clobbering a newer build. - `mergeBook()` overwrites existing entries by name (so reloading a book refreshes data). - Page-fill print pattern: `#page-X{display:flex; flex-direction:column; min-height:261mm}` + `.card.grow{flex:1}` + `.ta-print{flex:1}`. - autoGrow textareas (screen) + `.ta-print` mirror divs (print). - Headless Chrome verification (`--headless=new --print-to-pdf`/`--screenshot`/`--dump-dom`), pdftoppm, pypdf, PIL. - 5e rules math: AC by armor type/Unarmored Defense, encumbrance variant, Unarmored Movement, spell save DC, prepared-spell counts, hit dice. 3. Done. The fix was in the print stylesheet: `.card{break-inside:avoid}` plus the fixed-height flex layout were clipping any Features/Backstory text that ran past one sheet. I switched the three full-text pages (Features, Backstory, Notes) to a block layout with `break-inside:auto` and a one-page minimum height, so they fill at least a full sheet and then flow onto additional sheets as content grows.

Verified empirically by isolating each page and counting PDF pages:

|---|---|

| ~140 lines | 2 |
| ~260 lines | 3 |

So it stays at exactly one page until the content actually exceeds it, then spills onto a new overflow page (and another, and another). Backstory and Notes share the identical rule and behave the same.

text: What exactly *is* the build-data.py file and why is it separate from the HTML file itself?

blocks.text:
Good question — it's the one piece of this project that isn't the app itself. Here's the split:

## `Character Sheet.html` — the *program*
This is the whole application: the layout, the styling, and all the automation logic (ability math, AC, spell rules, the ASI flag, inventory weights, etc.). It is deliberately **content-free** — it ships with zero D&D game data baked in. Open it fresh and every box is empty; it knows the *rules* but not a single race, spell, or item. This is the file that lives in the public GitHub repo and is freely shareable.

## `build-data.py` — a *data-baking script* (run occasionally, not part of the app)
It's a Python command-line tool that:
1. Reads the raw 5etools JSON data sitting in your local `~/My Drive/5etools/data/` folder (races, classes, spells, items, backgrounds, feats…).
2. Trims and reshapes it into exactly the structures the sheet expects — this is where all those `build_races`, `build_classes`, `build_class_spells`, `bg_equipment`, cantrip-progression, etc. functions live.
3. Writes two outputs:
   - `source-data.json` — the processed content blob.
   - `Character Sheet (Source Data).html` — a **copy of the app with that content baked in**. This is the file you actually open to play with (it's why every change this session ends with me re-running the script and reopening that file).

## Why they're separate — it's a copyright wall

> The clean app stays shareable; the copyrighted WotC content never touches the public repo.

D&D's races/spells/items are **WotC's copyrighted content**. Owning the books covers your personal use, but not redistribution. So:

- `Character Sheet.html` (rules engine, no content) → **committed and shareable**.
- `source-data.json` and `Character Sheet (Source Data).html` (content baked in) → **gitignored, never committed**, regenerated locally by you via `python3 build-data.py`.

This is the same reason a change to the app only reaches your play copy after a rebuild — they're two different files by design.

## How it relates to the in-browser loader

There are actually **two** ways content gets in, doing the same job in two places:

- **`build-data.py`** — the *offline/CLI* path. Bakes a starter file in one shot.
- **The `et*` functions inside the HTML** (Settings → Source books) — the *in-browser* path. They fetch and process raw 5etools JSON from a local server live, so you can add books (XGE, TCE…) without running Python.

That's why this session keeps editing both `build-data.py` *and* the `et…` functions in the HTML together — they're parallel implementations of the same extraction, and both have to agree or a baked file and a browser-loaded file would differ.

So: the HTML is the engine, `build-data.py` is the (replaceable, personal-use) fuel pump. Keeping them apart is what lets the engine be open-source while the fuel stays your own.

blocks.text:
You're right — and it's worth separating two different "PHB" things, because one is a real limitation and the other is just cosmetic naming.

**Where PHB is a genuine functional hardcode (in `build-data.py`):**
- `PHB = "PHB"` + `is_phb(x)` — every extractor filters to `source == "PHB"`, so the script *only* ever pulls Player's Handbook content.
- `spells-phb.json` (filename regex) and `sources.json["PHB"]` (the class→spell map key) — both hardwired to the PHB files.
- `_meta.book = "Player's Handbook (2014)"`.

The in-browser loader (Settings → Source books) already moved past this — its `et*` functions take a source code and work for *any* book (XGE, TCE…). So `build-data.py` is the laggard: it's stuck baking only PHB, even though the architecture is otherwise book-agnostic.

**Where PHB is just leftover naming (cosmetic, no behavior):**
- The in-browser data global is literally named `PHB`, and the embedded data block is `<script id="phb-data">`, which `build_sheet` injects into. These work fine for any loaded book — the name is just a fossil. (The output file was already renamed to `source-data.json`.)

So the artifact is real, but "fixing" it splits into a low-risk functional change and a larger rename-everything cosmetic change. That's your call:

blocks.text:
Fixed and verified. Here's what was wrong and what to do.

**The bug:** When you load a book, subclasses were only attached to base classes *from that same book*. Order of Scribes is a **TCE** subclass but the **Wizard** it belongs to comes from the **PHB** — so it was being dropped on the floor. (Same was happening to every TCE subclass of a PHB class: Cleric's Order Domain, the TCE Sorcerer/Bard/etc. subclasses.) On top of that, `mergeBook` overwrote classes by name without merging their subclass lists.

**The fix (in `Character Sheet.html`):** the loader now collects every subclass in a book keyed by its parent class name, and `mergeBook` attaches them to the matching class that's already loaded — unioning subclass lists instead of overwriting. Verified: loading TCE onto PHB keeps all 8 PHB Wizard schools **and** adds Order of Scribes; Cleric gains Order Domain; Artificer comes in as a class.

**One catch for your current session:** your browser still has the *pre-fix* TCE data cached (and the picker now hides already-loaded books, so TCE won't reappear to re-load). To pick up the fix you need to clear the cached sourcebook once. In the sheet's browser console:

```js
localStorage.removeItem('dnd-sheet-sources'); location.reload();
```

Then TCE will be back in the **2014 ruleset** picker — load it again and Order of Scribes will be there.

Short answer: **the committed HTML carries no copyrighted *database* — but it does hardcode a handful of D&D names and rules formulas.** Whether that counts as "content-free" depends on where you draw the line. Here's exactly what I found:

## What's verified clean
- The embedded data block is literally `<script id="source-data">null</script>` — **zero baked catalog**: no races, no class data, none of the 361 spells, no descriptions, no item stats, no stat blocks. All of that lives only in the gitignored `source-data.json` / `(Source Data)` build.
- The two biggest lines in the file are the **paper-mini fold-guide SVGs**, which are from the open-source `dyslexic-charactersheets` project (credited in the README), not WotC.

## What *is* hardcoded (small, and arguably "rules math, not content")
**Game mechanics / formulas** — facts, the thing the README explicitly says the sheet automates:
- ASI level schedule `[4,6,8,12,14,16,19]` (Fighter), etc.
- Spell save DC `8 + prof + mod`; Unarmored Defense `10 + Con/Wis`; encumbrance thresholds; cantrips-known logic.

**A few specific names / one-liners** (the genuinely borderline bits):
- **Shadow Monk's fixed spell list** (`Minor Illusion, Darkness, Darkvision, Pass Without Trace, Silence`) + a paraphrased "Shadow Arts" note — `Character Sheet.html:1727`.
- **`FEAT_SENSES = { Observant: "+5 passive Perception & Investigation" }`** — `:1187`.
- The **"Monk (Way of Shadow)"** dropdown option and **"Mage Armor (13 + Dex)"**.
- Placeholder example text: `"Darkvision 60 ft, Observant feat, Danger Sense…"`.

## My read
Spell/feat/subclass **names are short titles** and **game mechanics are systems** — neither is the copyrightable *expression* (the creative flavor/description text is). So this sits inside the project's stated scope ("automates the rules math, not a content database"), and none of the bulk WotC content ships. By the strict letter of your "never commit copyrighted content" rule, though, those few hardcoded names are the only thing a purist could object to.

If you want maximal strictness, I can:
- Move the Shadow Monk fixed spell list and the Observant line **out of the HTML** and have them come from loaded data instead, leaving the committed file with mechanics-only.

text: I downloaded the HTML to my iphone and it isn't giving me the option to open it in a browser

blocks.text:
That's an iOS limitation, not a problem with the file. **Safari on iOS can't open local `file://` HTML** — tapping the `.html` in the Files app just gives you a Quick Look preview, which renders static HTML but won't reliably run the JavaScript or persist your character (no working `localStorage`). Apple sandboxes Safari away from local files.

You've got a few ways around it, easiest first:

**1. Documents by Readdle (free, App Store) — most reliable**
- Move/save `Character Sheet.html` into Documents.
- Tap it; it opens in Documents' built-in browser with full JavaScript and working `localStorage` (autosave persists), and you can use the sheet's **Save data file / Import** there too.
- Other equivalents that work: Koder, Textastic, a-Shell.

**2. Turn it into a real offline home-screen app (best long-term on iPhone)**
- Host the **content-free** `Character Sheet.html` (your repo is already public) on **GitHub Pages** → you get a URL.
- Open that URL in Safari → Share → **Add to Home Screen**. It then launches like an installed app, fully offline, with persistent autosave.
- Load your content on the phone via **Settings → Import file…** (a `source-data.json`), since the local 5etools server obviously isn't reachable from the phone.
- Caveat: you can't host the *data-baked* build — that's the copyrighted version — so the phone copy loads data via Import, not baked in.

**Why not just baked-HTML in Files:** even when Quick Look shows it, it's read-only-ish and won't keep your edits between sessions, so it's not a real way to play.

If you want, I can set up **GitHub Pages** for the repo so you've got a clean URL to "Add to Home Screen" — say the word and I'll enable it and confirm the link.

# BACKGROUNDS Data Pipeline Audit

Files: `~/My Drive/5etools/data/backgrounds.json` (raw), `~/Documents/dnd-character-sheet/build-data.py` (bake), `~/Documents/dnd-character-sheet/Character Sheet.html` (runtime parser + sheet).

## Raw schema (PHB, 20 backgrounds)
Per-background fields: `skillProficiencies`, `languageProficiencies`, `toolProficiencies`, `skillToolLanguageProficiencies`, `startingEquipment`, `entries` (a Feature block `name:"Feature: …"` + a "Suggested Characteristics" block holding d8/d6 Personality/Ideal/Bond/Flaw tables).

## Pipeline shape parity — PASS
`build_backgrounds` (build-data.py:172-183) and `etBackgrounds` (Character Sheet.html:1446-1452) emit the **identical** shape:
`{name, skills, skillChoose, feature:{name,text}, equip:{items,gold}}`.
The equipment helpers (`bg_equipment` py:157-170 / `etBgEquipment` html:1430-1445) are line-for-line equivalent: take all of `_`, else the first choice group; coin via `containsValue/100` copper→gp. No drift between bake-time and runtime. Good.

## Correctly handled
- **Skills → skill-prof checkboxes.** `applyBackground` html:2350 checks `skp-<key>` for each fixed skill. Severity: OK.
- **Feature → Features page.** html:2351-2354 appends `"<feat name> (<bg>). <text>"` to `#features`. Severity: OK.
- **Equipment + gold → inventory / currency.** `createCharacter` html:2588-2592 deposits `equip.items` via `addInvItem` and adds `equip.gold` to `#gp` (on top of class gold). Severity: OK.

## Available but DROPPED

### 1. Background TOOL proficiencies — DROPPED. Severity: HIGH
`toolProficiencies` is never read by the pipeline. `build_backgrounds`/`etBackgrounds` extract only `skillProficiencies`; there is no field for tools in the emitted object, and `applyBackground` (html:2346-2358) never touches `#proficiencies`. So Criminal's `thieves' tools` + gaming set, Folk Hero's artisan tool + `vehicles (land)`, Soldier's gaming set + vehicles, Sailor's `navigator's tools` + `vehicles (water)`, Charlatan's disguise/forgery kits, etc. all vanish.
Affects 12 of 20 PHB backgrounds. Asymmetry: races DO get this treatment (html:2320-2323 writes race langs into `#proficiencies`); backgrounds get nothing.

### 2. Background LANGUAGE proficiencies — DROPPED. Severity: HIGH
`languageProficiencies` (e.g. Acolyte/Sage `{anyStandard:2}`, Guild Artisan/Hermit/Noble/Outlander `{anyStandard:1}`) is never extracted. `applyBackground` does not write any "Languages: …" line into `#proficiencies`, even though the race path does exactly that and `etRaceLangs` (html:1393-1397) already contains reusable "N languages of your choice" formatting logic.
Affects 7 of 20 PHB backgrounds.

### 3. `skillChoose` for stock backgrounds — partially handled, but unreachable for choose-skill backgrounds. Severity: LOW (data-correct, near-dead path)
`skillChoose` IS extracted (`skills_from` py:147-155 / `etSkills` html:1384-1390) and surfaced as advisory text in `applyBackground` (html:2356, "Also choose N from …"). However, in PHB the only background with a skill choice is **"Custom Background" `{any:2}`**, and that form is NOT captured: `skills_from`/`etSkills` only recognize a literal `choose` key or `v===true` — the `{any:2}` shape falls through, so both `skills` and `skillChoose` come out empty for Custom Background's base entry. (The wizard's bespoke custom-bg panel sidesteps this with its own checkbox UI, so user impact is limited.) For real PHB stock backgrounds this is effectively moot since none use `choose`.

### 4. Personality / Ideal / Bond / Flaw suggestion tables — DROPPED. Severity: MEDIUM
The raw "Suggested Characteristics" block (d8 Personality Trait, d6 Ideal/Bond/Flaw tables) is never parsed. `build_backgrounds`/`etBackgrounds` only pick the entry whose name starts with `"Feature:"` (py:177-178 / html:1449); the characteristics block is discarded. The sheet HAS the destination fields — `#personality`, `#ideals`, `#bonds`, `#flaws` textareas (html:740-743) — but grep confirms nothing ever writes them programmatically. They're left blank for the user to fill manually. These are "suggested" (roll/pick) tables, so not strictly mechanical, but they are present in source and have dedicated sheet slots, so the drop is a genuine content gap.

### 5. `skillToolLanguageProficiencies` — DROPPED. Severity: LOW
A field present in the PHB schema (the Variant-rule "any one skill + any one tool/language" blocks). Not read anywhere in the pipeline. Low impact for the standard 20 PHB backgrounds but worth noting for completeness; it's the structured source for variant skill swaps.

## Note on the custom-background path (for contrast)
The wizard's custom-bg flow (html:2579-2585) is the ONLY place tools/languages reach `#proficiencies`: it joins the `.cbg-tl` select values into a line and appends them. This proves the sheet has the plumbing and target field — the stock `applyBackground` path simply doesn't use it. Fixing items 1-2 means extracting `toolProficiencies`/`languageProficiencies` in `build_backgrounds`+`etBackgrounds` and appending a line to `#proficiencies` in `applyBackground`, mirroring the race path at html:2320-2323.

Audit complete across all six domains. And yes — confirmed, everything below is scoped to **2014 ruleset only**; the agents filtered to `source=="PHB"`/classic and ignored all 2024 (XPHB/etc.) content, consistent with the book picker.

The headline: **the pipeline nails the "skeleton" (ability bonuses, speed, senses, HD, saves, skill choices, base class features, starting gear, AC/Dex math, item weights, packs, spell properties), but systematically drops two big categories** — (1) **proficiencies of every kind** granted by races/backgrounds/feats/classes, and (2) **a chosen feat's and subclass's actual mechanical effects.** A few fields are even extracted and then never rendered.

## Gaps by severity

### 🔴 High — real stats a player needs, currently missing or wrong
| Domain | Gap |
|---|---|
| **Feats** | Half-feat **ability increases** (Resilient/Observant/Durable/Actor…) are dropped → **final scores, mods, saves, skills, attacks are silently wrong**. Resilient's **save proficiency** and Skilled's **skill proficiencies** also dropped. A feat is just text in Features with *no* mechanical effect (and choice-feats have no UI to pick the ability). |
| **Races** | **Skill** (Elf→Perception, Half-Orc→Intimidation), **weapon** (Dwarf, elves), **armor** (Mountain Dwarf), and **damage resistances** (Dwarf/Tiefling/etc.) all dropped. **Dragonborn `_versions` is lost entirely** — no draconic ancestry, breath weapon, or resistance. |
| **Classes** | **Subclass features never added** to the sheet (subclass is just a label). **Subclass spells dropped** — domain/oath/Arcane-Trickster always-prepared spells never appear. **Warlock pact slots** not represented; **spells-known counts** never shown to known casters; **class tool profs** (Rogue thieves' tools) dropped. |
| **Backgrounds** | **Tool proficiencies** (12 of 20 backgrounds) and **language proficiencies** (7 of 20) dropped — even though the race path already writes languages to the Proficiencies box. |
| **Spells** | **Ritual tag absent** (31 PHB rituals have no indicator). |

### 🟡 Medium — present in data, would improve correctness/usability
- **Items:** weapon **damage/type/versatile/range** are fully extracted then **discarded** — selecting a weapon only writes its name; the Attacks table stays manual. Armor **stealth disadvantage** and **strength-requirement speed penalty** extracted but ignored (the sheet already has the Stealth row + STR-speed machinery to act on them).
- **Spells:** **higher-level scaling text** is extracted as `higher` then **never rendered** (easy win — just append to the tooltip); **concentration** isn't a distinct flag; costly **material components** (Revivify 300gp) dropped.
- **Backgrounds:** Personality/Ideal/Bond/Flaw suggestion tables never fill the existing sheet fields.
- **Classes:** `casterProgression`/`casterAbility`/`preparedSpells` are extracted but ignored (logic is hardcoded in the `CASTERS` map instead).

### 🟢 Low — cosmetic/forward-looking
Feat prerequisites (no eligibility filter), `scalingLevelDice`, casting-time `condition`, age/height tables, `traitTags`.

**Cross-cutting root cause:** proficiency arrays (`skillProficiencies` / `toolProficiencies` / `languageProficiencies` / `weaponProficiencies` / `armorProficiencies`) exist on races, backgrounds, feats, and classes but are dropped at the **extraction** layer for most of them. A single shared fix — extract those arrays everywhere + one `applyProficiencies()` routine that checks skill boxes and appends weapon/armor/tool/language lines to the Proficiencies box — closes the majority of the High-severity items at once.

There's a lot here, and some fixes need UI decisions (feat ability sub-choice picker, Attacks auto-fill, ritual badge). Rather than unilaterally make dozens of changes, let me confirm scope:

def _merge_prof(a, b):   # union two prof blocks (base race + subrace), preserving order, dedup
    out = {}
    for k in ("skills", "tools", "languages", "weapons", "armor", "other"):
        merged = list((a or {}).get(k, [])) + list((b or {}).get(k, []))
        if merged: out[k] = list(dict.fromkeys(merged))
    ch = (a or {}).get("skillChoose") or (b or {}).get("skillChoose")
    if ch: out["skillChoose"] = ch
    return out

        bases[r["name"]] = {"ability": ab, "speed": _speed(r), "traits": _traits(r.get("entries", [])), "featGrants": fg, "prof": pf, "resist": rs}

DnD Beyond handles this by having an additional "Active" toggle for weapons to get them added to the Attacks table. How is that, or do you have any better ideas?

blocks.text:
Good instinct — auto-adding from inventory is too aggressive. The DnD Beyond "Active" toggle is a solid model and I'd lean that way, with one wrinkle worth deciding up front.

The wrinkle: our Attacks table has a **manual attack-bonus column** (DnD Beyond auto-computes it). So a two-way toggle is clean for name + damage, but the question is whether deactivating should also wipe a bonus you hand-typed. My take: yes — "Active" should mean "this weapon's attack lives in the Attacks table"; toggling off removes that whole row (matching DDB semantics), and toggling on re-adds it fresh. That keeps it predictable.

I'll also first **remove** the current behavior (weapons auto-populating Attacks just by being in inventory).

blocks.text:
Grounded numbers: the Monster Manual has **450 monsters** (100 of them beasts), ~1.5 MB raw; all bestiary books together are ~11 MB. So "everything" is very doable, but it means a new **bestiary** data category and real file-size growth (a trimmed MM ≈ +0.6–1 MB on the baked file). Monsters would load when you load a bestiary book (the Monster Manual) via Source books — I'd extend the loader to also pull `bestiary-*.json`, since right now it only grabs races/classes/spells/items.

## My take on Wild Shape

I'd **not** make it a third page. Animal Companion, Familiar, Pact of the Chain, summons, *and* Wild Shape are all the same underlying thing for a sheet: **"render a chosen monster stat block, with a template that tweaks it."** Wild Shape is literally "you become this beast's stat block (keeping your mental stats)" — same machinery as a companion.

So my recommendation is a single **"Companions & Forms"** page that can hold **multiple** creature blocks, each with: a searchable stat-block picker, a template dropdown, current-HP tracking, notes, and a portrait. That way one page covers a Ranger's beast companion *and* their owl familiar, or a Druid's several Wild Shape forms — and Wild Shape is just the template on one of those blocks. Cleaner than two/three near-identical pages.

## How it'd work
- **Stat-block picker:** a searchable typeahead (native `datalist`, no dependencies) over every monster in your loaded bestiary books — mouse to ancient dragon. Picking one fills a monster stat block (AC, HP, speed, 6 abilities + mods, saves, skills, senses, CR, prof bonus, traits, actions).
- **Templates:** Find Familiar, Pact of the Chain, Beast Master Animal Companion, Wild Shape, generic Summon/Polymorph — each applies its deterministic rule changes where they're well-defined (e.g., Wild Shape keeps your Int/Wis/Cha; Animal Companion adds your prof bonus to its rolls/AC and scales HP) plus a rules note for the rest.
- **Portrait → Mini:** each creature's portrait generates its own fold-up mini alongside your character's.
- **Pen-and-paper:** blank picker + labeled stat boxes you can hand-fill, same principle as the rest of the sheet.

This is a sizable multi-phase build (data extraction + loader + the new page + picker + templates + Mini), so I want to lock the architecture before writing it. Three decisions:

blocks.name: AskUserQuestion

questions.question: Where should Wild Shape live?

options.label: Template on the shared page (Recommended)
options.description: Wild Shape is one of the templates on the Companions & Forms page. Reuses all the same stat-block machinery; a Druid can pre-stat several forms as separate blocks. No third page.

options.label: Dedicated third stat page
options.description: A separate Wild Shape page after the companion page. More tabs, but keeps 'you transformed' visually distinct from 'creatures you command.'

questions.question: How many creature blocks should the page hold?

options.label: Multiple, add/remove (Recommended)
options.description: Hold several creature blocks on the page (companion + familiar + multiple wild-shape forms). Each is its own stat block + template + portrait. More flexible; a bit more build.

options.label: Single creature slot
options.description: One creature at a time; re-pick to change it. Simpler, smaller, but can't hold a companion and a familiar simultaneously.

questions.question: How much should templates automate?

options.label: Auto-apply deterministic rules + notes (Recommended)
options.description: Where the rules are unambiguous (Wild Shape keeps mental stats; Animal Companion adds prof bonus & scales HP; familiar telepathy/can't-attack), apply them automatically; surface the rest as a rules note.

options.label: Notes/overlay only
options.description: Templates just attach the relevant rules text; you apply the changes by hand. Simplest and least error-prone, but less automated.

blocks.text: Now mirror the same tag improvements in `build-data.py`'s `render_tags`:

blocks.name: Edit

input.old_string:
# ---- 5eTools {@tag ...} markup -> plain text ----
_tag = re.compile(r"\{@(\w+) ([^{}]*)\}")
def render_tags(s):
    if not isinstance(s, str): return s
    prev = None
    while prev != s:
        prev = s
        def repl(m):
            tag, body = m.group(1), m.group(2)
            parts = body.split("|")
            if tag in ("dice","damage","scaledamage","scaledice","d20","hit","dc","filter"):
                return parts[0]   # @filter is {display|page|filters...} — display is parts[0], not parts[2]
            if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[2].strip():   # explicit display text
                return parts[2]
            return parts[0]
        s = _tag.sub(repl, s)
    return s
input.new_string:
# ---- 5eTools {@tag ...} markup -> plain text ----
_tag = re.compile(r"\{@(\w+)(?: ([^{}]*))?\}")
_ATK = {"mw":"Melee Weapon Attack","rw":"Ranged Weapon Attack","mw,rw":"Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack",
        "ms":"Melee Spell Attack","rs":"Ranged Spell Attack","ms,rs":"Melee or Ranged Spell Attack"}
def render_tags(s):
    if not isinstance(s, str): return s
    prev = None
    while prev != s:
        prev = s
        def repl(m):
            tag, body = m.group(1), m.group(2) or ""
            parts = body.split("|")
            if tag == "h": return "Hit: "                                  # monster damage-line marker
            if tag == "atk": return (_ATK.get(body.strip(), body)) + ":"
            if tag == "hit": return parts[0] if parts[0][:1] in "+-" else "+" + parts[0]
            if tag == "dc": return "DC " + parts[0]
            if tag == "recharge": return f"(Recharge {parts[0]}-6)" if parts[0] else "(Recharge 6)"
            if tag in ("dice","damage","scaledamage","scaledice","d20","filter"):
                return parts[0]   # @filter is {display|page|filters...} — display is parts[0], not parts[2]
            if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[2].strip():   # explicit display text
                return parts[2]
            return parts[0]
        s = _tag.sub(repl, s)
    return s

blocks.text:
The Animal Companion feature is fully built, tested, and pushed across four commits (`5eded8f`, `e8aa256`, `c369d94`, `a467366`).

## What you've got

**A "Companions & Forms" page** (between Spells and Background) that holds **multiple** add/remove creature blocks. Each block has:

- **A searchable stat-block picker** — type-ahead over *every* monster in your loaded bestiary books (mouse → ancient dragon → air elemental). Picking one auto-fills a full editable stat block: AC, HP + current, speed, six abilities with live mods, saves/skills/senses/resist/immune/etc., CR, prof bonus, and traits/actions/reactions/legendary/spellcasting as text.
- **A template dropdown** that auto-applies the deterministic rules + a note:
  - **Find Familiar** / **Pact of the Chain** — form list + can't-attack / can-attack notes
  - **Beast Master Animal Companion** — adds your prof bonus to AC, sets HP to max(normal, 4×level)
  - **Wild Shape** — keeps your Int/Wis/Cha and prof bonus, uses the beast's physical stats
  - **Summon / Polymorph** — generic
- **A portrait** that generates its own captioned fold-up paper mini next to your character's on the Mini page.
- Everything stays editable and is **blank-but-writable** for pen-and-paper, and persists with the character.

**On Wild Shape:** it's a template on this shared page (your choice), so a Druid can stat several forms as separate blocks — no third page.

## One thing to know
Monsters come from **loading the Monster Manual** (Settings → Source books → Monster Manual → Load) — that pulls in all 450 stat blocks. The clean repo stays content-free; the bestiary is copyrighted WotC data that lives only in your loaded/baked copy, same as spells/items. `DATA_VERSION` bumped to 11, so stored sourcebooks refresh on next load.

# Browser Render (flash-free HTML → image)

When you need to render a local HTML/SVG file to a PNG or PDF to inspect it (e.g. checking how a generated page, character sheet, or report looks), do NOT launch Chrome with `--headless=new`. On macOS that mode spins up a real GPU/window surface and produces a visible **white screen flash** on every launch. In a tight render→check→fix loop that strobes the whole display every few seconds and reads, to the user, like something is repeatedly taking a screenshot. (This was the cause of a real "my screen keeps flashing" report on 2026-06-03 — a render loop on the D&D character sheet.)

Important: the flash is purely cosmetic — headless Chrome screenshots a **file**, never the user's actual screen, so there is no privacy/capture concern. But it is alarming and unnecessary. Use a flash-free path.

## Preferred: `--headless=old`

One-flag change. The legacy headless mode renders fully offscreen (no window surface, no flash):

```bash
CHROME="/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"
"$CHROME" --headless=old --disable-gpu --no-first-run \
  --user-data-dir=/tmp/render-$$ --hide-scrollbars \
  --window-size=1000,1400 --screenshot=/tmp/out.png \
  "file:///tmp/page.html"
```

Verified to still produce a PNG on Chrome 148 (2026-06-03), even though old headless was nominally removed around Chrome 132 — the flag is still honored. **Caveat:** confirmed it *renders*; the no-flash behavior was not visually self-verified (can't see the screen from a tool). If you switch a loop to `--headless=old` and the user still reports flashing, Chrome is likely aliasing `old`→`new` on their version — fall back to Playwright below.

## Robust fallback: Playwright (best for JS-heavy pages)

If `--headless=old` still flashes, or the page needs real JS execution / interaction (clicking tabs, waiting on load), use Playwright's true-headless Chromium — it does not create an on-screen window on macOS:

```bash
# one-time: pip install playwright && playwright install chromium
python3 - <<'PY'
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch()                 # headless by default, no flash
    pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width":1000,"height":1400})
    pg.goto("file:///tmp/page.html")
    pg.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
    # pg.click('.ptab[data-page="spells"]')  # real interaction if needed
    pg.screenshot(path="/tmp/out.png", full_page=True)
    b.close()
PY
```

## Other options (static HTML only, no JS)

- `qlmanage -t -s 1400 -o /tmp "/tmp/page.html"` — macOS Quick Look, native, no flash, but ignores most JS.
- `wkhtmltoimage page.html out.png` — old WebKit, offscreen, no flash; weak JS. (`brew install --cask wkhtmltopdf`)

## Cleanup

Each Chrome render leaves a throwaway `--user-data-dir` and PNG in `/tmp`. Use a unique dir per call (e.g. `/tmp/render-$$`) and sweep stale ones afterward:

```bash
rm -rf /tmp/render-* /tmp/cs* /tmp/cnd*   # stale headless profiles
```

## Rule of thumb

Default to `--headless=old`. Reach for Playwright when the page is JS-driven or the flash persists. Never leave a raw `--headless=new` in a loop that runs while the user is at the machine.

blocks.result:
1	# Universal D&D 5e Character Sheet
2	
3	A single, self-contained, **automated** D&D 5e (2014 rules) character sheet that runs in any
4	web browser with **no install, no server, no internet, and no Adobe, while also functioning as a beautiful pen-and-paper sheet**. The whole app — layout,
5	styling, and automation — lives in one file: `Character Sheet.html`.
6	
7	## Why a single HTML file?
8	The most universal runtime on any device (Windows, Mac, Linux, iPhone, Android, ChromeOS) is the
9	web browser. A self-contained `.html` with inlined CSS + JavaScript depends on nothing external,
10	works fully offline, and will keep working for years. It replaces MPMB's Adobe-locked automation
11	with the same kind of live calculation, in a runtime everyone already has.
12	
13	## Use it
14	1. Double-click `Character Sheet.html` (opens in your default browser).
15	2. Fill it in. Everything recalculates live:
16	   - ability modifiers, proficiency bonus (from level), saving throws,
17	   - all 18 skills (with **proficiency** and **expertise** toggles), passive perception,
18	   - initiative, and a "10 + Dex" helper for AC.
19	3. **Ability scores** — the Abilities card shows only the final **score** and **modifier**. Click
20	   **⚙ Under the hood** (hidden when printing) for everything that feeds them:
21	   - **Generation method** — **Manual** (type base scores), **Standard Array** (assign 15/14/13/12/10/8,
22	     each used once), or **Point Buy** (27-point budget, scores 8–15, with a live points counter).
23	   - **Bonus columns** — separate **ASI**, **Racial**, **Magical**, and **Misc** bonuses per ability,
24	     plus a **Notes** field. Final score = base + ASI + racial + magical + misc.
25	   Creating a character auto-fills the Racial column from the chosen race.
26	3. It **auto-saves to that browser** as you type — reopening the file restores your character.
27	4. **Portrait** — click the empty box by the name to upload one (png/jpeg/webp/heic/etc.); it fits
28	   to the header height. Click an uploaded image for a pop-up menu: **Replace / Download original /
29	   Remove**. The original file is stored so the download is full resolution. HEIC is kept and
30	   re-downloadable but only previews in Safari. The image is saved under its own key so a large photo
31	   can't break the rest of autosave (very large images may not persist locally — use Save to keep them).
32	
33	## Pages
34	Tabs at the top switch pages on screen; **printing outputs every page on its own sheet**.
35	1. **Core** — identity, abilities, saves, skills (left), combat, attacks, a Limited Features
36	   tracker (Feature / Max / Recover LR·SR·Dawn / Used), and Proficiencies & Languages (right).
37	2. **Inventory** — currency (PP/GP/EP/SP/CP) with coin weight, an item table with total weight, and
38	   Strength-based carrying capacity (Encumbered ×5, Heavily ×10, Max Carry ×15, Push/Drag/Lift ×30)
39	   with a live status, plus an Equipment & Notes box.
40	3. **Features** — Features & Traits (background features land here).
41	3b. **Background** — appearance (age/height/weight/eyes/skin/hair) + Personality / Ideals / Bonds / Flaws.
42	3c. **Backstory** — Character Backstory, Allies & Organizations, Notes.
43	4. **Spells** — pick a spellcasting class and the spell list adapts along two axes:
44	   - **Pre-populates the full class list** (Cleric/Druid/Paladin) — every class spell is listed with a
45	     Prep checkbox; others (Wizard/Bard/Sorcerer/Warlock/Ranger) are blank rows you write into.
46	   - **Shows a Prep column** for classes that prepare daily (Wizard + the full-list classes); known
47	     casters (Bard/Sorcerer/Warlock/Ranger) just list their spells (always ready).
48	   Auto Spell Save DC (8 + prof + mod) and attack bonus, slot totals (1–9), and cantrips. The
49	   "include spell sheet" checkbox (for non-casters) never prints.
50	5. **Mini** — auto-builds a print-and-fold paper mini (fold-over standee) from the character
51	   **portrait**: a front panel, an auto-flipped back panel (so it reads upright once folded over the
52	   top crease), and a 3-step cut/fold/glue instruction guide. Needs a portrait; the page hides itself
53	   (and won't print) when there's none, or uncheck "Include paper mini" to skip it. Self-contained —
54	   the fold-guide and instruction art are inlined SVGs, no internet needed. Adapted from the
55	   open-source [dyslexic-charactersheets](https://github.com/dyslexic-charactersheets) "Map Minis".
56	
57	## Pen & paper
58	A fresh sheet (before "Create Character" is used) is completely empty — no scores, no `0`/`+0`
59	computed values, just blank boxes — and the free-write areas are sized for handwriting. So you can
60	print a blank copy and fill it in by hand. Fill any value digitally and the math fills itself in.
61	
62	## Toolbar
63	- **Create Character** → guided wizard (Race → Class/Subclass/Level → **class skill choices** →
64	  **starting equipment or gold** → Background → ability method → name) that fills the sheet: race
65	  bonuses/speed/senses, class saves/hit dice/spell list, chosen skill proficiencies, and either the
66	  class's starting gear (into Equipment Notes) or average starting gold (into Currency). Needs
67	  sourcebook data loaded (baked into the build, or loaded via Settings).
68	- **Save** → downloads a self-contained copy of the sheet with your character (and portrait) baked
69	  in. Email / AirDrop / Drive it; opening that copy anywhere shows the character. This is the way to
70	  move a character between devices (auto-save is per-browser localStorage, not written to the file).
71	- **Print / PDF** → "Save as PDF". A dense, standardized stylesheet fits a normal character onto
72	  **one page** (builder UI hidden; text sections render as full-content mirrors; two balanced columns).
73	- **Settings** → page-layout toggles (hide/show any tab) and **Source books** (see below).
74	- **New** → opens a fresh blank character in a new tab (current one untouched). Each tab gets its own
75	  storage slot via a `#slot=…` URL hash; the loaded sourcebook is shared across slots.
76	- **Reset** (red) → after confirmation, clears *this* sheet back to defaults (deletes the character
77	  and portrait in place). The loaded sourcebook is kept.
78	
79	## Source books (Settings)
80	Open **Settings → Source books** to load D&D content. Two ways:
81	- **From a local 5etools server** — pick any book (PHB, XGE, TCE, …) and click **Load**. The sheet
82	  fetches the raw 5etools JSON from your server (default `http://localhost:5050`, editable) and
83	  processes it **in the browser** (a JS port of `build-data.py`). Loading more books **merges** them
84	  (dedup by name), so you can stack sources. Works fully offline as long as that local server is
85	  running — nothing is fetched from the internet.
86	- **Import file…** — load a pre-built `source-data.json` (made by `build-data.py`) when you don't
87	  want to run a server.
88	- **Save data file** — a browser can't overwrite the file it's opened from, so this **downloads an
89	  updated copy** of the sheet (`Character Sheet (Source Data).html`) with **every loaded book baked
90	  into the file**. Keep it / replace your sheet with it to make the books permanent and portable.
91	Loaded data is also remembered per browser (localStorage). It is **copyrighted WotC content for
92	personal use** — it lives only in your browser / your own file and is never committed; the shipped
93	app stays content-free.
94	
95	`New` clears the character from the current browser (export first if you want to keep it).
96	
97	## Scope
98	- **Rules:** D&D 5e **2014** ruleset only. 2024 ("One D&D") books are filtered out of the in-browser
99	  book picker on purpose — this sheet is built for the 2014 rules.
100	- **Pages:** identity, abilities, saves, skills, combat, attacks, limited-features tracker,
101	  proficiencies, inventory (weight/currency math + carrying capacity), features, background, backstory,
102	  notes, spellcasting (slots + prepared/known + auto save DC / attack), and a print-and-fold mini.
103	- **Guided creation** with sourcebook data, plus live rules-math automation for any character.
104	
105	## Roadmap
106	- **A separate 2024-compliant sheet.** The 2024 ruleset changes enough (backgrounds grant ASIs and a
107	  feat, weapon mastery, new spell prep, species vs. race, etc.) that it warrants its own sheet rather
108	  than bolting onto this one. The book picker already classifies 2014 vs 2024, so the 2024 set is ready
109	  to feed a future sheet.
110	- TTS / audio readout of a character; richer multiclass spell-slot math.
111	
112	## Sourcebook data (personal use)
113	There are two ways to get content into the sheet (see **Source books** above): load any book live
114	from a local 5etools server in-browser, or bake a starter file with `build-data.py`, which extracts a
115	trimmed subset (races, backgrounds, classes, feats, weapons/armor, spells) from a local 5eTools copy
116	into `source-data.json` and bakes it into `Character Sheet (Source Data).html`. It defaults to the
117	**Player's Handbook (2014)**; pass a 5eTools source code to extract a different book:
118	
119	```
120	python3 build-data.py            # Player's Handbook (2014) — the default
121	python3 build-data.py XGE        # Xanathar's Guide to Everything
122	```
123	
124	This is **copyrighted WotC content** included for personal use under ownership of the books. Owning a
125	book does not grant redistribution rights, so `source-data.json` and any sheet with data baked in
126	(`Character Sheet (Source Data).html`, or anything you make with **Save data file**) are
127	**gitignored and must not be shared/committed**. The clean app (`Character Sheet.html`) stays
128	content-free and remains freely shareable.
129	
130	## Design / longevity rules
131	Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS only — no frameworks, no build step, no CDN, no web-fetched fonts (uses the
132	system font stack). Edit it with any text editor. Data model is plain JSON keyed by field id.

## Pages
Tabs at the top switch pages on screen; **printing outputs every page on its own sheet**. Hide any
page you don't want via **Settings → Layout**.
1. **Core** — identity & portrait; abilities (final score + modifier, with a **⚙ Under the hood**
   generator); saving throws; 18 skills; senses & passive perception; hit dice; and Proficiencies &
   Languages. The combat area holds Proficiency Bonus, Inspiration, AC / Initiative / Speed / HP /
   Death Saves, a free-form **Resistances / Immunities / Defenses** box, an **Attacks** table (with a
   calculated *attacks per action* from Extra Attack), and a **Limited Features** tracker
   (Feature / Max / Recover / Used).
2. **Inventory** — currency (PP/GP/EP/SP/CP) with coin weight; a 34-row item table (auto item weights,
   drag to reorder, live total weight); Strength-based carrying capacity (×5/×10/×15/×30 with status);
   **Armor** (sets your AC, with AC-bonus item pickers) beside **Attuned Items**; and Equipment Notes.
3. **Features** — Features & Traits. Class, subclass, racial, feat, and background features all land
   here on character creation.
4. **Spells** — pick a spellcasting class and the sheet tailors itself: cantrips-known and
   spells-known/preparable counts, the visible spell levels, and the slot tracker all scale to your
   class & level (full / half / one-third / Warlock pact). Each row is a dropdown of your class's
   spells; hovering a spell shows its full text, with a **ritual** marker, material components, and
   "at higher levels" scaling. Auto Spell Save DC and attack. Supports subclass casters (Eldritch
   Knight, Arcane Trickster, Way of Shadow monk).
5. **Companions & Forms** — animal companions, familiars, summons, and **Wild Shape** forms. Add
   multiple creature blocks, each with a searchable monster stat-block picker (load the Monster Manual

1	# Universal D&D 5e Character Sheet
2	
3	A single, self-contained, **automated** D&D 5e (2014 rules) character sheet that runs in any
4	web browser with **no install, no server, no internet, and no Adobe, while also functioning as a beautiful pen-and-paper sheet**. The whole app — layout,
5	styling, and automation — lives in one file: `Character Sheet.html`.
6	
7	## Why a single HTML file?
8	The most universal runtime on any device (Windows, Mac, Linux, iPhone, Android, ChromeOS) is the
9	web browser. A self-contained `.html` with inlined CSS + JavaScript depends on nothing external,
10	works fully offline, and will keep working for years. It replaces MPMB's Adobe-locked automation
11	with the same kind of live calculation, in a runtime everyone already has.
12	
13	## Use it
14	1. Double-click `Character Sheet.html` (opens in your default browser).
15	2. Fill it in. Everything recalculates live:
16	   - ability modifiers, proficiency bonus (from level), saving throws,
17	   - all 18 skills (with **proficiency** and **expertise** toggles), passive perception,
18	   - initiative, AC (from the armor you select), hit dice, spell save DC / attack, spell slots,
19	     carrying capacity / encumbrance, and effective speed.
20	3. **Ability scores** — the Abilities card shows only the final **score** and **modifier**. Click
21	   **⚙ Under the hood** (hidden when printing) for everything that feeds them:
22	   - **Generation method** — **Manual** (type base scores), **Standard Array** (assign 15/14/13/12/10/8,
23	     each used once), or **Point Buy** (27-point budget, scores 8–15, with a live points counter).
24	   - **Bonus columns** — separate **ASI**, **Racial**, **Magical**, and **Misc** bonuses per ability,
25	     plus a **Notes** field. Final score = base + ASI + racial + magical + misc.
26	   Creating a character auto-fills the Racial column from the chosen race.
27	4. It **auto-saves to that browser** as you type — reopening the file restores your character.
28	5. **Portrait** — click the box by the name to upload one (png/jpeg/webp/heic/etc.); it's shown at a
29	   fixed size beside the name. Click an uploaded image for a pop-up menu: **Replace / Download original /
30	   Remove**. The original file is stored so the download is full resolution. HEIC is kept and
31	   re-downloadable but only previews in Safari. The image is saved under its own key so a large photo
32	   can't break the rest of autosave (very large images may not persist locally — use Save to keep them).
33	
34	## Pages
35	Tabs at the top switch pages on screen; **printing outputs every page on its own sheet**. Hide any
36	page you don't want via **Settings → Layout**.
37	1. **Core** — identity & portrait; abilities (final score + modifier, with a **⚙ Under the hood**
38	   generator); saving throws; 18 skills; senses & passive perception; hit dice; and Proficiencies &
39	   Languages. The combat area holds Proficiency Bonus, Inspiration, AC / Initiative / Speed / HP /
40	   Death Saves, a free-form **Resistances / Immunities / Defenses** box, an **Attacks** table (with a
41	   calculated *attacks per action* from Extra Attack), and a **Limited Features** tracker
42	   (Feature / Max / Recover / Used).
43	2. **Inventory** — currency (PP/GP/EP/SP/CP) with coin weight; a 34-row item table (auto item weights,
44	   drag to reorder, live total weight); Strength-based carrying capacity (×5/×10/×15/×30 with status);
45	   **Armor** (sets your AC, with AC-bonus item pickers) beside **Attuned Items**; and Equipment Notes.
46	3. **Features** — Features & Traits. Class, subclass, racial, feat, and background features all land
47	   here on character creation.
48	4. **Spells** — pick a spellcasting class and the sheet tailors itself: cantrips-known and
49	   spells-known/preparable counts, the visible spell levels, and the slot tracker all scale to your
50	   class & level (full / half / one-third / Warlock pact). Each row is a dropdown of your class's
51	   spells; hovering a spell shows its full text, with a **ritual** marker, material components, and
52	   "at higher levels" scaling. Auto Spell Save DC and attack. Supports subclass casters (Eldritch
53	   Knight, Arcane Trickster, Way of Shadow monk).
54	5. **Companions & Forms** — animal companions, familiars, summons, and **Wild Shape** forms. Add
55	   multiple creature blocks, each with a searchable monster stat-block picker (load the Monster Manual
56	   via Source books) and a template (Find Familiar, Pact of the Chain, Beast Master, Wild Shape, …).
57	   Each creature's portrait also makes its own paper mini.
58	6. **Background** — appearance (age/height/weight/eyes/skin/hair) + Personality / Ideals / Bonds /
59	   Flaws + Allies / Enemies.
60	7. **Backstory** — a full-page Character Backstory box.
61	8. **Notes** — a full-page free-text box.
62	9. **Mini** — print-and-fold paper minis (fold-over standees) built from the character **portrait**
63	   and every companion portrait: a front panel, an auto-flipped back panel (so it reads upright once
64	   folded over the top crease), and a cut/fold/glue guide. The page hides itself (and won't print)
65	   when no portrait exists. Self-contained inlined SVG art. Adapted from the open-source
66	   [dyslexic-charactersheets](https://github.com/dyslexic-charactersheets) "Map Minis".
67	
68	## Pen & paper
69	A fresh sheet (before "Create Character" is used) is completely empty — no scores, no `0`/`+0`
70	computed values, just blank boxes — and the free-write areas are sized for handwriting. So you can
71	print a blank copy and fill it in by hand. Fill any value digitally and the math fills itself in.
72	
73	## Toolbar
74	- **Create Character** → guided wizard (Race → Class/Subclass/Level → **class skill choices** →
75	  **starting equipment or gold** → Background → ability method → name) that fills the sheet from the
76	  loaded sourcebook data: race ability bonuses / speed / senses / damage resistances / languages;
77	  class saves, hit dice, and spellcasting; **all proficiencies** (skills checked, weapons/armor/tools/
78	  languages listed); class **and** subclass **features**, plus a subclass's always-prepared spells;
79	  **limited-use resources** (Rage, Ki, Sorcery Points, Channel Divinity, …) into the Limited Features
80	  tracker with hover descriptions; and either the class's starting gear (resolved into Inventory, with
81	  choice/category/pack prompts) or average starting gold. Backgrounds deposit their items + gold too.
82	  Needs sourcebook data loaded (baked into the build, or loaded via Settings).
83	- **Save** → downloads a self-contained copy of the sheet with your character (and portrait) baked
84	  in. Email / AirDrop / Drive it; opening that copy anywhere shows the character. This is the way to
85	  move a character between devices (auto-save is per-browser localStorage, not written to the file).
86	- **Print / PDF** → "Save as PDF". A dense, standardized stylesheet fits a normal character onto
87	  **one page** (builder UI hidden; text sections render as full-content mirrors; two balanced columns).
88	- **Settings** → page-layout toggles (hide/show any tab) and **Source books** (see below).
89	- **New** → opens a fresh blank character in a new tab (current one untouched). Each tab gets its own
90	  storage slot via a `#slot=…` URL hash; the loaded sourcebook is shared across slots.
91	- **Reset** (red) → after confirmation, clears *this* sheet back to defaults (deletes the character
92	  and portrait in place). The loaded sourcebook is kept.
93	
94	## Automation highlights
95	Beyond character creation, the sheet keeps these live as you edit:
96	- **Ability Score Improvements & feats** — a flag tracks every ASI you're owed (by class & level,
97	  including Fighter/Rogue extras and race-granted feats like Variant Human) and won't clear until you
98	  pick an ASI or a feat for each. Half-feats apply their ability bump, save/skill proficiencies, etc.
99	- **Attacks** — toggle a weapon's **Atk** box in Inventory to add it to the Attacks table with an
100	  auto-computed attack bonus and damage; ability substitutions are handled (Monk Martial Arts → Dex,
101	  Hexblade → Cha, Battle Smith → Int). A calculated *attacks per action* reflects Extra Attack.
102	- **Spell slots** auto-fill (and lock) for any known single-class caster (full / half / one-third /
103	  Warlock pact); multiclass and "Other" stay manual and writable.
104	- Race / background / feat / class **proficiencies** route to the skill checkboxes and the
105	  Proficiencies box; the **Observant** feat also adds its line to Senses.
106	
107	## Source books (Settings)
108	Open **Settings → Source books** to load D&D content. Two ways:
109	- **From a local 5etools server** — pick any book (PHB, XGE, TCE, **Monster Manual**, …) and click
110	  **Load**. The sheet fetches the raw 5etools JSON from your server (default `http://localhost:5050`,
111	  editable) and processes it **in the browser** (a JS port of `build-data.py`). Loading the Monster
112	  Manual brings in every monster stat block for the **Companions & Forms** page. Loading more books
113	  **merges** them (dedup by name), so you can stack sources. Works fully offline as long as that local
114	  server is running — nothing is fetched from the internet. Only 2014-ruleset books are listed (2024
115	  books are filtered out); already-loaded books drop out of the picker.
116	- **Import file…** — load a pre-built `source-data.json` (made by `build-data.py`) when you don't
117	  want to run a server.
118	- **Save data file** — a browser can't overwrite the file it's opened from, so this **downloads an
119	  updated copy** of the sheet (`Character Sheet (Source Data).html`) with **every loaded book baked
120	  into the file**. Keep it / replace your sheet with it to make the books permanent and portable.
121	- **Clear loaded books** — forgets anything loaded in this browser and reverts to the data baked into
122	  the file (use it to re-load a book with refreshed data). Your character isn't affected.
123	Loaded data is also remembered per browser (localStorage). It is **copyrighted WotC content for
124	personal use** — it lives only in your browser / your own file and is never committed; the shipped
125	app stays content-free.
126	
127	`New` clears the character from the current browser (export first if you want to keep it).
128	
129	## Scope
130	- **Rules:** D&D 5e **2014** ruleset only. 2024 ("One D&D") books are filtered out of the in-browser
131	  book picker on purpose — this sheet is built for the 2014 rules.
132	- **Pages:** Core (abilities/saves/skills/senses/combat/resistances/attacks/limited features/
133	  proficiencies), Inventory (weight & currency math, carrying capacity, armor, attunement),
134	  Features, Spells (slots + prepared/known + auto save DC / attack), Companions & Forms, Background,
135	  Backstory, Notes, and a print-and-fold Mini.
136	- **Guided creation** with sourcebook data, plus live rules-math automation for any character.
137	
138	## Roadmap
139	- **A separate 2024-compliant sheet.** The 2024 ruleset changes enough (backgrounds grant ASIs and a
140	  feat, weapon mastery, new spell prep, species vs. race, etc.) that it warrants its own sheet rather
141	  than bolting onto this one. The book picker already classifies 2014 vs 2024, so the 2024 set is ready
142	  to feed a future sheet.
143	- TTS / audio readout of a character; richer multiclass spell-slot math.
144	
145	## Sourcebook data (personal use)
146	There are two ways to get content into the sheet (see **Source books** above): load any book live
147	from a local 5etools server in-browser, or bake a starter file with `build-data.py`, which extracts a
148	trimmed subset (races, backgrounds, classes + subclasses, feats, weapons/armor, spells, and monster
149	stat blocks) from a local 5eTools copy into `source-data.json` and bakes it into
150	`Character Sheet (Source Data).html`. It defaults to the **Player's Handbook (2014)**; pass a 5eTools
151	source code to extract a different book:
152	
153	```
154	python3 build-data.py            # Player's Handbook (2014) — the default
155	python3 build-data.py XGE        # Xanathar's Guide to Everything
156	python3 build-data.py MM         # Monster Manual (monster stat blocks for companions)
157	```
158	
159	This is **copyrighted WotC content** included for personal use under ownership of the books. Owning a
160	book does not grant redistribution rights, so `source-data.json` and any sheet with data baked in
161	(`Character Sheet (Source Data).html`, or anything you make with **Save data file**) are
162	**gitignored and must not be shared/committed**. The clean app (`Character Sheet.html`) stays
163	content-free and remains freely shareable.
164	
165	## Design / longevity rules
166	Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS only — no frameworks, no build step, no CDN, no web-fetched fonts (uses the

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: The overarching project is a single self-contained, offline, no-Adobe D&D 5e (2014 rules) character sheet (`Character Sheet.html`), with copyrighted PHB/5etools content kept strictly out of the public repo. This session was a long series of feature additions and refinements. In chronological order the explicit requests were: - Make the Backstory box auto-expand with its text like Features (was already working). - Both Features and Backstory pages should overflow onto a new page in real time if needed (print pagination). - The "Can Prepare" box should be available/writable when no spellcasting class is selected; only hide it for an actively-selected non-prepared caster. - Carrying-capacity boxes too squished → make them taller/writable (twice). - Add "Monk (Way of Shadow)" as a spellcasting class with its fixed Shadow Arts spell selection, non-prepared; then: no extra blank rows; no spell-slots tracker; fix leftover "Minor Illusion" when switching class away. - Every spell row should be a dropdown of all spells available to that class at that level — "for all the classes that have to learn spells. Not the ones who already have all relevant spells." - Item Wt column should show the line total (qty × per-item) and change with quantity. - Race-granted feats (Variant Human, etc.) should also prompt the ASI alert window. - Backgrounds should deposit their provided items and gold into inventory at creation. - The Observant feat should auto-populate into the Senses box. - Cantrip slot count should match cantrips-known at the level (if a level is denoted). - (Conceptual) What is build-data.py / why separate from the HTML? → Then: the PHB reference is an artifact; "Generalize + rename fossils." - "Pick a book" dropdown: separate 2014 vs 2024 ruleset → then "filter out 2024 entirely. We will make a separate 2024-compliant sheet at a later time.
