It should be some kind of calculated value in the Attacks box." → then: must be a labeled writable box for pen-and-paper. - Move Spells page after Features but before Background. - Create an Animal Companion sheet (after Spells, before Background): searchable list of every monster stat block, templates (familiar, pact of the chain, etc.), portrait → Mini; Wild Shape decision (chose: template on shared page, multiple creature blocks, auto-apply deterministic templates). - Proceed with Warlock Pact-slot auto-fill and EK/AT spellcasting. - Limited-use-per-day abilities (Ki, Sorcery Points, Bardic Inspiration, etc.) auto-populate the Limited Features card with hover tooltips. - Move the Armor section to the Inventory page, side-by-side with Attuned Items (stack attuned vertically). - Set up Resistances/Immunities in the Combat card (dropdowns for damage with resistance/immunity indicator, condition-immunity dropdowns, free-form notes box). - Narrow the Combat + Proficiency Bonus + Inspiration cards and put Resistances in the freed right space. - Change Resistances to just a free-form text box labeled "Resistances/Immunities/Defenses"; squish its width so PB/Inspiration/Combat grow back out for handwriting. - "Update the readme" (most recent completed request). 2. blocks.text:
Fixed and pushed (`bd7a9be`). Xanathar's now loads fully.

The root cause was deeper than the two bugs I fixed earlier — those were correct, but **the load was throwing before it ever reached them**, so it looked like nothing changed. Running the page's actual JS in Node (against your live 5etools server) surfaced two more:

2. **Subclasses loaded featureless.** The in-browser loader was building its class data from only the `class` and `subclass` arrays, silently dropping `classFeature`/`subclassFeature`. def build_items(raw, items=None):
    weapons, armor = [], []
    for it in raw.get("baseitem", []):
        if not is_src(it): continue
        if it.get("weapon"):
            weapons.append({"name": it["name"], "cat": "martial" if it.get("weaponCategory")=="martial" else "simple",
                            "melee": it.get("type") == "M",
                            "dmg": it.get("dmg1",""), "dmgType": DMG.get(it.get("dmgType",""), it.get("dmgType","")),

                            "props": [WPROP.get(p, p) for p in (it.get("property") or [])],
                            "range": it.get("range","")})
        elif it.get("armor") or it.get("type","") in ("LA","MA","HA","S"):
            armor.append({"name": it["name"], "ac": it.get("ac"), "type": it.get("type",""),
                          "stealth": bool(it.get("stealth")), "strength": it.get("strength")})
    # named magic armors (Elven Chain, Dwarven Plate, ...) live in items.json, not baseitem
    for it in (items or {}).get("item", []):
        if not is_src(it): continue
        ty = (it.get("type") or "").split("|")[0]
        if ty in ("LA","MA","HA") and it.get("ac") is not None:
            armor.append({"name": it["name"], "ac": it.get("ac"), "type": ty,
                          "stealth": bool(it.get("stealth")), "strength": it.get("strength")})

- **All items for every book live in the same `items.json` / `items-base.json` files**, each tagged with its `source`. My loader reads those and filters by the book you're loading, then `mergeBook` unions the results — so whatever 2014 book you load contributes its items. - **Weightless containers are detected the same way** (via 5etools' `containerCapacity.weightless` flag, filtered by source). Across the entire 2014 ruleset the weightless containers are: Bag of Holding, Heward's Handy Haversack, and Quiver of Ehlonna (all DMG), plus **Heward's Hireling Armor** from Lost Laboratory of Kwalish (LLK). Load LLK and that one works as a container too; if any future-loaded book defines a new weightless container, it'll be picked up automatically — nothing is hardcoded to specific items.

One caveat: a handful of adventure-module items exist only as lore (`fluff-items.json`) without real stats — those won't appear, since they have no item entry. But anything with an actual stat block in the loaded book will.

So load any 2014 book and its items become available to add, and any container it defines just works. No code change needed — the design already handles it.

text: So I just need to reload the DMG and the fix will apply to all items from all books?

blocks.text:
No — reloading the DMG only refreshes the **DMG's** items. The item catalog and container detection are computed per-book at load time, so each book carries its own items, and `mergeBook` unions them. A book you loaded *before* these fixes still has its old, item-less data until you reload **that** book.

So:

- **Reload the DMG** → you get the DMG's ~515 items in autocomplete + its weightless containers (Bag of Holding, Handy Haversack, Quiver of Ehlonna), and the Elven Chain/magic-armor fixes.
- **Items from Xanathar's, Tasha's, etc.** won't appear in autocomplete until you reload *those* books too — reloading the DMG doesn't reprocess them.

Two ways to get everything current:

1. **Reload each book** you've loaded, one at a time, via the new Reload picker. (Most surgical.)
2. **Clear loaded books**, then load them all fresh. (Simplest if you only have a couple — every book gets processed with the new code in one pass.)

Two prerequisites either way:
- You must be running the **latest `Character Sheet.html`** (the file itself has to contain the new code — if you're opening an older saved copy, reloading data won't help).
- If your PHB comes from a baked file rather than the server, re-bake it (or load PHB from the server) so its items get the new treatment too.

So the rule of thumb: **the new processing applies to a book only when that book is (re)loaded with the updated code** — it's not retroactive across already-loaded books.

Fix: added a consistent **8px gap** to those page containers, aligned `.stack` to 8px too, and gave the other multi-card pages (Spells, Background, Companions) the same flex-column gap so the principle applies everywhere.

Verified by rendering the print PDF: page 1 now has a clean gap between the header and the columns with all cards evenly separated, and the inventory page cards are distinctly spaced like the rest.

Done and pushed (`fa40c9f`). I pivoted from the in-place row-growth approach to the dedicated **Overflow page** you described.

**What it does:**
- A new **Overflow** tab/page holds a **second full inventory list (34 rows)** and an **extra 8-row Limited Features list**.
- These aren't separate silos — they're the *same* systems extended: total **68 inventory rows** (34 main + 34 overflow) and **16 Limited Features rows** (8 on Core + 8 overflow). So weight totals, the Equip checkboxes, containers, drag-and-drop (now wired across both grids, including cross-page), the item search box, and the auto-fill all carry over to the overflow rows.
- **Limited Features (automatic):** the auto-fill flows into the overflow rows once the Core card's 8 are full — no action needed.
- **Inventory (manual):** you just type or search into the overflow rows as normal.

**Print:** the Overflow page prints on its own sheet **only when it's actually used** (it's excluded when empty, exactly like the Mini page, re-checked right before printing). I also caught and fixed a CSS bug where the page-spacing rule's ID specificity was overriding the "hide excluded page" rule.

Verified end-to-end: rows 0–67 and limited 0–15 exist; the Overflow page renders 17+17 inventory columns plus 8 limited rows; an empty overflow is excluded from the PDF (dropped it from 12 → 11 pages, with Notes as the last sheet) and reappears once anything is added.

text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The overarching project (continuing from prior sessions) is a single self-contained, offline, no-Adobe D&D 5e (2014 rules) character sheet — `Character Sheet.html` — with a Python extractor `build-data.py` that pulls trimmed copyrighted 5etools data into gitignored files. The public repo (BaesTheorem/dnd-character-sheet) must remain content-free. This session was a sequence of discrete bug fixes and features, each requested explicitly:
   - Fix "Xanathar's still isn't loading."
   - Squish the Combat card width; top-align Armor Class/Initiative; stack Death Save Failures under Successes and center-align "Failures"; fix the print Resistances card placement; give the print "Attacks" header parity.
   - Add a Material/Enchantment armor modifier (Mithral/Adamantine/+1/+2/+3); include named magic armors (Elven Chain) — must apply to all loaded books; fold magic armor `bonusAc` into AC (Elven Chain = 16).
   - Make loaded source books re-loadable (then a separate reload picker, then a one-click "Reload all loaded sources" button; drop the redundant loaded-book name list).
   - Inventory: add items from sourcebooks (searchable), make Bag of Holding/Handy Haversack function as weight-ignoring containers; make the item picker substring-searchable; make containers collapsible; remove the "In" column; containers shouldn't indent unless nested; container contents move with the container when dragged.
   - Equipped items adding AC bonuses auto-fill the "Item (adds to AC)" list, gated behind attunement; "Make the Inventory the only pipeline for items" — change ATK checkbox to "Equipped" for weapons/armor/magic/attunement items; Armor + Attunement dropdowns list only equipped qualifying items.
   - Mage Armor only in the armor dropdown if on the spell list; "Unarmored" always available.
   - Background-selected languages go on the SAME line as race languages.
   - Spells sorted alphabetically within their level sections.
   - Auto-add class features / equipped items / feats with limited daily uses to "Limited Features" (Lucky, Order of Scribes features, Ki, Sorcery Points, Bag of Tricks, etc.).
   - Apply consistent print card spacing to all cards (esp. inventory page).
   - Custom Lineage skill-or-darkvision choice + race language selection prompts in the wizard.
   - Feat effects applied (Resilient save proficiency + half-feat +1; Alert +5 initiative + Senses).
   - Investigate the 46 of 121 limited-use items that didn't auto-detect.
   - Create a dedicated Overflow page for inventory/limited-features spillover; then expand it: also accommodate Features overflow, default layout = 8 Limited Features rows + remaining space split 50/50 between inventory and features, plus a way to manually create more overflow pages.
   - Fix Limited Features detection for Awakened Spellbook (1/LR), Manifest Mind/Master Scrivener/One With the Word (1/LR), and exclude Spellcasting (LAST request, completed).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Vanilla single-file HTML/CSS/JS; localStorage autosave (KEY, SOURCES_KEY="dnd-sheet-sources"); `<script id="source-data">` baked data; in-browser global `DATA`.
   - `build-data.py` (Python extractor; default PHB, `SRC_TAG`) kept in lockstep with in-browser `et*` mirror functions; `DATA_VERSION`.
   - In-browser book loading: `fetch5etoolsBook(base, srcCode)` fetches `/data/*.json` from a local 5etools server (default http://localhost:5050) and processes via `et*` functions; `mergeBook(into, add, bookName)` unions/overwrites by name and unions string-arrays.
   - 5etools data quirks: cross-book subclasses carry `classSource`=base book (use `subclassSource`); class spells added via `classVariant` not just `class`; `additionalSpells` per-level values can be nested objects; magic armor `bonusAc`; `containerCapacity.weightless`; `reqAttune`; item `rarity`.
   - Save/load: `collect()` gathers `[data-save]` + custom arrays (invUnits, invConts, invEquip, lfDesc, atkLinks, companions) + scalars (collapsed, overflowPages); `applyAll(data)` → `applyFields(data)` + restores.
   - `compute()` runs on every input; calls refreshEquipToggles, refreshEquippedPickers, renderAcItems, renderContainers, refreshLimitedFeatures.
   - Dynamic counts: `let NINV, NLIMITED, overflowPages`; rows built via `invRowHTML(i)`/`limitedRowHTML(i)`; overflow pages appended dynamically.
   - Testing: Node `vm` harness (Proxy DOM shims + real fetch) for pure-data logic; headless Chrome `--headless=old --dump-dom` with `--virtual-time-budget` and `document.title` channel for DOM/compute logic; `--print-to-pdf` + Read PDF pages for print.
   - browser-render skill: use `--headless=old` (not `--headless=new`) to avoid screen-flash; Playwright not installed.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `~/Documents/dnd-character-sheet/Character Sheet.html` — the entire content-free app; nearly all edits land here. Key current structures:
     - Constants: `const NATTACKS=5; const INV_MAIN=34, OV_INV=24; const NSPELLROWS=24; const LIM_MAIN=8, OV_LIM=8; let NINV=INV_MAIN, NLIMITED=LIM_MAIN, overflowPages=0;` plus module-level `invRowHTML(i)` and `limitedRowHTML(i)`.
     - Overflow machinery: `overflowPageHTML(k)` (section with Limited Features card on top + `.overflow-split` grid of Inventory card + Features & Traits textarea `featov-${k}` + `[data-addoverflow]` button), `appendOverflowPage()`, `removeOverflowPages()`, `setOverflowPages(n)`, `overflowPageUsed(k)`. Tab ids `overflow-${k}`, page ids `page-overflow-${k}`, tbodies `limov-${k}`/`invov-${k}`. `applyLayout()` excludes empty overflow pages; `setOverflowPages(data&&data.overflowPages)` runs in `applyAll` before `applyFields`; `data.overflowPages=overflowPages` in collect; `[data-addoverflow]` click handler appends + showPage + save + compute; `beforeprint`→`applyLayout`.
     - CSS: `.overflow-split{display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:16px; align-items:stretch; flex:1 1 auto}` + `.overflow-split>.card{margin:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column}` + textarea flex; print rule `#page-spells:not(.excluded), #page-bg:not(.excluded), #page-companion:not(.excluded), .page[data-page^="overflow-"]:not(.excluded){display:flex !important; flex-direction:column; gap:8px}`.
     - Limited Features detection (MOST RECENT edit): `LIMITED_FEAT_NAMES` (from LIMITED_RESOURCES), plus new `const LIMITED_EXCLUDE = new Set(["spellcasting","pact magic"]);` and `const LIMITED_OVERRIDES = {"awakened spellbook":{max:"1",rec:"LR"}, "manifest mind":{max:"1",rec:"LR"}, "master scrivener":{max:"1",rec:"LR"}, "one with the word":{max:"1",rec:"LR"}};`. `lfIndexByName(name)` helper. `refreshLimitedFeatures()`:
       ```
       featureBlocks().forEach(b => {
         const lc = b.name.toLowerCase();
         if(LIMITED_FEAT_NAMES.has(lc)) return;
         if(LIMITED_EXCLUDE.has(lc)){ const i = lfIndexByName(b.name); if(i>=0){ /*clear lfname/lfmax/lfrec/lfused + remove title*/ } return; }
         if(LIMITED_OVERRIDES[lc]){ const o=LIMITED_OVERRIDES[lc], i=lfIndexByName(b.name); if(i>=0){ lfmax=o.max; lfrec=o.rec; } else addLimitedRow(b.name,o.max,o.rec,...); return; }
         const r = limitedFromText(b.name, b.text); if(r) addLimitedRow(...);
       });
       // then equipped items via DATA.itemText + limitedFromText
       ```
       `limitedFromText(name,text)` heuristic: requires a recovery (short/long rest→SR/LR, dawn→Dawn, per day→1/Day) AND a usage signal (countRe `\b(\d+)\s+(?:charges|uses|luck points|ki points|sorcery points)\b`, expend/spend, regain expended, "once|twice|three times|N times" not multiplier, `can(?:'t|not) ?be used\b[^.]{0,25}\bagain\b`, "number of times equal to"); max from countRe or `\d+ times`. `addLimitedRow` auto-appends an overflow page when full.
     - `LIMITED_RESOURCES` map (class resources Rage/Ki/Sorcery Points/etc. with computed counts) → `fillLimitedFeatures` at createCharacter.
     - Inventory: container assignment on `$("invname-i").dataset.cont` (rowCont/setRowCont); collapse toggle on the drag handle (`.invdrag.cont-toggle`); nested rows indent via `.in-container td.invitem{padding-left:14px}` + ↳ in `.cont-caret`; `moveInvBlock` moves a container with its contents; drag handlers bound across all `.inv-cols` (overflow inv is a plain table, no drag). Item search `setupItemSearch` (prefix-first ranking, cap 200, scroll).
     - AC: `acItemsState()` (equipped AC-bonus items, attunement-gated), `renderAcItems()`, `hasEquippedShield()`; armor modifier (mithral/adamantine/+N) in compute AC block; `armorByName`/`magicSet`/`attuneSet`/`equippedNames`/`refreshEquippedPickers` (armor dropdown = equipped LA/MA/HA only; Mage Armor only if `hasSpellNamed("Mage Armor")`; attune slots = equipped attune items).
     - `addLanguages(langs)` consolidates all language sources onto one deduped `Languages:` line.
     - Race: `etRaces` adds `darkvision`/`langChoose`/`variableSkillDarkvision`; `renderRaceChoices()` (Custom Lineage skill/darkvision radio + language dropdowns); `applyRace(name, opts)`.
     - Feats: `applyAsiBonuses` applies save proficiencies ungated (idempotent); `FEAT_SENSES` (Observant, Alert), `FEAT_INIT={"Alert":5}`, `featInitBonus()` added to Initiative.
   - `~/Documents/dnd-character-sheet/build-data.py` — mirrors: `build_classes`/`build_class_spells` (subclassSource/classVariant), `_collect_spell_names`, `build_items`(+items.json magic armor with bonusAc fold), `build_item_names`, `build_containers`, `build_attune_items`, `build_magic_items` (MAGIC_RARITY), `build_item_text` (limited-use magic items, `txt[:1600]`, LIMITED_SIGNAL pre-filter), `build_races` (darkvision/langChoose/variableSkillDarkvision), `lang_choose`. `DATA_VERSION` bumped earlier.
   - Gitignored (never commit): `source-data.json`, `Character Sheet (Source Data).html`.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - XGE not loading: (a) `prep[lv].forEach is not a function` (Sun Soul resource spells) → recursive `_collectSpellNames`/`_collect_spell_names`; (b) `classAll={class:[],subclass:[]}` dropped feature arrays → added `classFeature`/`subclassFeature` collection (subclasses were loading featureless). Also earlier `subclassSource` (not classSource) and `classVariant` spell routing.
   - Elven Chain showed AC 15 not 16: extractor ignored `bonusAc`; fold `ac + bonusAc`.
   - Shields appeared in the base-armor dropdown after redesign: filtered `refreshEquippedPickers` armor list to LA/MA/HA only (shields stay equippable + AC-bonus items).
   - Search "cuts off after the I's": `filter().slice(0,50)` over alphabetical list → prefix-first ranking + cap 200 + scroll.
   - Drag-onto-container above an item was a no-op (moveInvRow from===to skipped save/compute) → added explicit save()+compute() after the branch; this also fixed collapse/attune persistence cascade.
   - Empty Overflow page still printed: print rule `#page-overflow{display:flex !important}` (ID specificity) overrode `.page.excluded{display:none !important}` → scoped flex rule with `:not(.excluded)`.
   - Limited features detection: 46/121 items missed — ~25 correct exclusions (incidental words, consumables, duration limits), ~21 genuine (truncation at 800 → bumped to 1600; "can't be used this way again" → loosened pattern); improved to 95/121.
   - Limited features misfires (LAST): Awakened Spellbook blank/SR, Spellcasting false-positive, Manifest Mind/Master Scrivener/One with the Word — fixed with LIMITED_OVERRIDES (1/LR) + LIMITED_EXCLUDE (spellcasting/pact magic), and refreshLimitedFeatures now clears stray excluded rows and corrects override rows in place (preserving Used).
   - Tooling: `timeout` not on macOS (used background+kill); headless `--dump-dom` doesn't capture async/setTimeout without `--virtual-time-budget`; `document.title` grep flakiness mitigated by reading DOM files directly.
   - User feedback/direction changes: user scrapped the attune auto-add approach in favor of "Inventory the only pipeline" (Equipped checkbox); user pivoted mid-implementation from in-place row growth to a dedicated Overflow page; then expanded the Overflow page spec (8 limited + 50/50 inventory/features + manual add-page).

5. Problem Solving:
   Diagnosed deep load crashes by running the page's real JS in Node against the live server. Built a robust dynamic-page system (overflow pages) with grow-only/append semantics and save/load round-trips. Balanced a fuzzy text heuristic for limited-use detection with a curated override/exclude layer for known features. Maintained one-page print fit and consistent card spacing. Repeatedly verified end-to-end in the real browser engine before committing.

6. All user messages:
   - "Xanathar's still isn't loading"
   - "Please squish the width of the combat card as far to the left as it can go while still keeping the labels of all the boxes on a single line."
   - "\"Armor Class\" and \"Initiative\" need to be pushed to the top of their respective boxes"
   - "Death Save failures should be positioned right under successes, line up their respective check boxes."
   - "The word \"Failures\" should be center-aligned with \"Successes\""
   - "The print view of page 1 shows the Resistances/Immunities/Defense squished way off to the right. Please ensure it looks more like the tab view."
   - "The print view's \"Attacks\" header hasn't been given parity with the other section headers like the tab view version was"
   - "Where is the Elven Chain shirt?"
   - "I already loaded the DMG, and the Elven Chain shirt isn't available."
   - "Commit and push" (multiple times)
   - "I need an easy way to re-load an already loaded source book."
   - "Put already loaded books into a separate picker for re-loading."
   - "The current plain text list of loaded books is now redundant"
   - "With the Elven Chain's +1 bonus to AC, I should have a 16 AC right?"
   - "I need to be able to add items from the source books inventory. Additionally, I need the Handy Haversack and Bag of Holding to function as containers I can put other items into, which ignores the weight of the contained items."
   - "Will this apply to items in other source books as well?"

Done and committed (`a0fca58`). There's now a small, unobtrusive **"+ Add spell sheet"** button at the bottom of the Spells page. Clicking it adds an entirely new, self-contained spell page — its own **"Spells 2"** tab, class picker, ability, Spell Save DC / Attack, slot tracker, and full spell table — so you can host another class's list without touching your first.

What I did under the hood (it was a real refactor, not just a button):
- **Instance-namespaced the whole spell subsystem.** Sheet 0 keeps its original element IDs (so existing saved characters load unchanged); each extra sheet suffixes every ID with `__1`, `__2`, etc.
- State moved from the old `spellEntries`/`preparedSpells`/`spellMaxLevel` globals to per-sheet arrays, and all the render/slot functions now take a sheet index. `compute()` loops every sheet for DC/attack/prepared counts; spell-row edits and the class picker route to the right sheet.
- **Save/load** round-trips the new arrays + sheet count, and legacy single-sheet saves still load straight into sheet 0.
- **Print:** an empty extra sheet is excluded from printing (like overflow pages); a used one flows across sheets normally.

Verified end-to-end in the real engine: adding a sheet, two classes side by side (Wizard write-in rows vs. Cleric pre-filled list), independent slot auto-fill (both L5 → 4/3/2), a full save→reload round-trip preserving both classes and a per-sheet spell entry, and the visual render above.

blocks.text:
Done, committed and pushed (`caf5b58`).

Now when a race, background, or feat grants an **unspecified "artisan's tools of your choice"** or **"musical instrument of your choice"**, creating the character (or closing the feat/ASI picker) opens a **"Choose Your Tools"** modal with a dropdown per grant, populated with the actual options (the 17 artisan's tools / 10 instruments from your loaded books). Your pick is written straight into the Proficiencies & Languages box.

Details:
- **Specific grants are left alone** — "Thieves' Tools", "Smith's Tools", etc. don't trigger a prompt; only the generic "of your choice" phrasing does.
- **Surrounding text is preserved** — the source tag (e.g. "(Entertainer)") and the rest of the line stay; only the generic phrase is replaced.
- **Multi-count grants** (e.g. a Bard's "two musical instruments of your choice") offer one dropdown each and join the picks.
- **Graceful fallback** — if no sourcebook with tool data is loaded, it just leaves the generic text (no empty prompt).

Implementation: tools are now categorized (`DATA.toolCats` = {artisan, instrument}) in both the live loader and `build-data.py` (`build_tool_cats`), merged across books, with `DATA_VERSION` bumped to 12. A `resolveToolChoices()` scanner finds generic phrases and opens the modal; `applyToolChoices()` splices the chosen names back in.

Verified end-to-end against regenerated PHB data: 17 artisan tools + 10 instruments categorized, the modal opens with the right selects, "Artisan's Tools of your choice" → "Smith's Tools", "2 musical instruments of your choice" → "Lute, Drum", and "Thieves' Tools" untouched. Pushed to `origin/main` (`4377ee3..caf5b58`); only the app + builder were committed (sourcebook data stays gitignored).

And yes, the existing math is correct per 5e (2014), which is why it's worth leaving alone:

- **Max Carry (carrying capacity) = STR × 15** — the most you can carry, shown as "Max Carry ×15"

That's multi-agent-workflow territory (it'll spawn many agents and use a lot of tokens), so I want your call on scope before running it.

Here's what my server-wide recon already established so I don't re-tread it:
- **Extraction is generic** — races, classes, subclasses, features, spells, items, monsters all flow through book-agnostic code, so most non-PHB content already lands correctly.
- **Fixed now:** the "any N skills" picker (Bard + several races/backgrounds).

All pushed, working tree clean. Here's the audit outcome.

## What the audit found
Six dimension auditors swept your loaded sources against the sheet's extraction/handling code. The extraction pipeline is generic (handles any book), but several **systemic** patterns were broken. I fixed the correctness-affecting ones and verified each against your live 5etools server.

## Fixed & verified (5 commits, pushed)

**Race abilities** (the biggest gap — ~65 of ~101 race entries were silently missing bonuses)
- "Choose" floating bonuses (Half-Elf, Variant Human, Custom Lineage, Simic Hybrid, SCAG Tieflings…) now have a **picker in the Race step**.
- The ~52 free-assign races (MPMM/Tasha: Goliath, Tabaxi, Orc, Genasi…) get a **+2/+1 picker**. *(Verified: Variant Human +1/+1, Half-Elf Cha+2 + chosen, Goliath +2/+1.)*

**Spellcasting**
- Cross-book class spell lists no longer dropped (the granting-book filter bug) → **Artificer** is now a full prepared caster with its real list; cross-book additions land. *(Artificer 95 spells, Cleric 114.)*
- Subclass **always-prepared** spells get checked/added on the Spells page; **expanded** lists (Warlock patrons) surface. *(Fiend expanded = 10.)*
- **Racial** cantrips/innate spells (Tiefling, Drow…) surface as a "Racial Spells" line.

**Limited Features** — Max now resolves for **proficiency-bonus** and **ability-modifier** scaling and **once-per-rest** single-use features; added **Artificer** (Flash of Genius, Spell-Storing Item); "Channel Divinity: X" options no longer spawn duplicate rows.

**Special AC** — **Natural Armor** races (Lizardfolk/Loxodon/Tortle/…), **Draconic Resilience** + **Dragon Hide** (13+Dex), and **Warforged** (+1) now compute right. *(Lizardfolk AC 15, Warforged 13.)* **Alternate speeds** (fly/swim/climb/burrow) surface in Senses.

**Skills** — "any N skills" picker (Bard + floating-skill races). All mirrored in `build-data.py`; smoke test passes with no JS errors.

## Remaining (rated HIGH by the audit, but lower urgency — these still appear as editable text in the Proficiencies/Languages box, so nothing is *silently wrong*)
- **Background language choices** (Acolyte/Sage "2 languages of your choice", etc.) — need a wizard picker (currently literal text on the Languages line).
- **Gaming-set / thieves'-tools** choices — the tool picker only covers artisan's tools + instruments; other tool choices show as text.
- Minor: Monk's tool *OR*-choice flattens to two; Rogue/Bard **Expertise** isn't auto-prompted; language standard-vs-exotic isn't filtered.

Want me to do the proficiency-selection pickers (background languages + gaming-set tools) next? That'd close the last of the HIGH items.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The current active request: "Please do another audit of all the loaded classes and races to make sure that each one has all of its abilities properly extracted and listed in the appropriate spot in the character sheet, and that any special modifications they need are made to any calculations." Clarified across follow-ups: "No I meant all the OTHER stuff I have loaded in since." / "I have a ton of other sources we need to prepare the sheet for." / "At least the 16 sources I have loaded currently." — i.e., the audit must cover the user's ~16 LIVE-loaded 5etools sourcebooks (not just PHB), ensuring extraction completeness and special calculation handling. When asked how to scope the exhaustive audit, the user chose "Multi-agent workflow."

   Earlier completed requests in this window (all committed/pushed): move Reset into a "General" settings tab; hide Companions page until a creature is added (like Mini); larger fit-to-size companion portraits that print; blank Features page prints a full-page write-in card; prompt to pick specific artisan's tools/musical instrument for generic grants; default the "+ Add spell sheet" button off and merge Spells+Source-books settings into an "Advanced" tab; when variant Encumbrance is off, fit all 4 Carrying Capacity boxes on one row; add a dedicated inventory delete (✕) button; fix Chain Mail AC; remove Lay on Hands from Limited Features; list duplicate rolled stat values; revert the auto-armor-select fix (selecting armor must stay a manual dropdown step) while keeping case-insensitive armor matching; add a General-settings toggle for the variant Encumbrance rule (default off, removing the 3 encumbrance references from the Inventory sheet when off).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Single-file vanilla HTML/CSS/JS character sheet; localStorage autosave; print via @media print → one page per tab.
   - In-browser `et*` extraction functions (etRaces, etClasses, etClassSpells, etSkills, etProfBlock, etNormProf, etFeats, etSpeed, etToolCats, _collectSpellNames, _clean, _titlecase) mirrored by `build-data.py`. The user loads books LIVE via fetch5etoolsBook from localhost:5050, so the in-browser et* functions are what matter for their data; build-data.py is for baked/offline default (PHB).
   - 5etools data quirks: spell `sources.json` class links carry the GRANTING book's source (not the spell's book); subclass additionalSpells use prepared/known/innate/expanded keys; spell name refs carry `|source` and `#level` tags; races use fixed ability bonuses, `choose` floating blocks, or no ability block (Tasha/MPMM free-assign); natural armor; alternate speeds (fly/swim/climb/burrow as numbers or `true`).
   - CASTERS table (fullList/prepares/ability/note), SUB_CANTRIPS, SPELL_LIST_FROM, LIMITED_RESOURCES (computed counts), limitedFromText heuristic + LIMITED_OVERRIDES/LIMITED_EXCLUDE, resolveLimMax/pbValue sentinels.
   - Multi-sheet spells (instance-namespaced, spellEntriesByInst/preparedByInst), wizard steps (0 Race, 1 Ability Scores, 2 Class, 3 Skills, 4 Equipment, 5 Background, 6 Name), renderRaceChoices (rc-* pickers), applyRaceAbilityOnly/applyRace (keepRacial).
   - Verification: headless Chrome `--headless=old --dump-dom` with `--virtual-time-budget`, `document.title` channel; loading books via `mergeBook(DATA, await fetch5etoolsBook('http://localhost:5050', code), code)`; print-to-PDF + Read PDF.
   - Workflow tool (multi-agent, requires explicit opt-in — user gave it): 6 parallel read-only dimension auditors returning structured `{dimension, summary, gaps:[{area,detail,severity,fix}]}`.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `Character Sheet.html` (main app — all in-browser fixes):
     - `renderWizSkills` — fixed "any N skills" (Bard + races): falls back to all 18 skills when count>0 and from empty: `const list = (ch.from && ch.from.length) ? ch.from.map(...) : SKILLS.map(([k,label]) => ({key:k, label}));` hint `Choose ${ch.count}${(ch.from&&ch.from.length)?"":" from any skill"}.`
     - `etClassSpells` — removed `if(c.source === SRC)` filter on `.class` links so cross-book/Artificer lists populate: `(sourcesForSrc[name].class||[]).forEach(c => { (out[c.name]=out[c.name]||[]).push({n:name, l:lv}); });`
     - CASTERS Artificer → `{fullList:true, prepares:true, ability:"int", note:"...pre-filled..."}`.
     - `etClasses` subclass spells — added `expanded`: collects `blk.expanded` into `expanded` array; `arr.push({name, short, features, spells, expanded})`.
     - `_collectSpellNames` (unchanged) + new `etRaceSpellNames(r)` walking known/innate/prepared → cleaned names.
     - `etRaces` — added `spells: etRaceSpellNames(r)` and `speedExtra: etSpeedExtra(r)` to base, nameless-subrace merge, and named subrace.
     - `etSpeedExtra(r)` — non-walk modes as "fly N ft., swim N ft." (true→walk).
     - `_clean` → `etTags(String(s)).split("|")[0].split("#")[0].trim()` (strips #level tags).
     - `applyRace` — surfaces racial spells as a "Racial Spells. Granted by your race: ..." feature line; `if(r.speedExtra) addSense("Other speeds: " + r.speedExtra);`
     - `createCharacter` subclass-spell block — marks always-prepared subclass spells: `if(sInfo && sInfo.fullList) subObj.spells.forEach(sp => { preparedByInst[0][sp.n] = true; });` else write-in caster pushes prepared rows into spellEntriesOf(0); surfaces `expanded` as text; `if(spellKey) renderSpellStyle(false, 0);`
     - `resolveLimMax` — handles `"PB"` (pbValue) and `/^(str|dex|con|int|wis|cha)mod$/` → `String(Math.max(1, modOf(...)))`.
     - `limitedFromText` — Max resolution: explicit digit; `/number of times equal to your proficiency bonus/`→"PB"; `/number of times equal to your (strength|...) modifier/`→`am[1].slice(0,3)+"mod"`; word counts (three times→3, twice→2); `can(?:'t|not) ?(?:be )?used?...again`→"1"; returns `{name, max: resolveLimMax(max), rec}`.
     - LIMITED_RESOURCES — added `Artificer:[{name:"Flash of Genius",rec:"LR",feat:"Flash of Genius",min:7,count:(l,m)=>Math.max(1,m.int||0)},{name:"Spell-Storing Item",rec:"LR",feat:"Spell-Storing Item",min:11,count:(l,m)=>2*Math.max(1,m.int||0)}]`.
     - `refreshLimitedFeatures` — added skip: `if(/^channel divinity\b\s*[:(]/.test(lc)){ const i=lfIndexByName(b.name); if(i>=0) clearLfRow(i); return; }`
     - `const NATURAL_ARMOR = { "lizardfolk":{base:13,stat:"dex"}, "locathah":{base:13,stat:"dex"}, "loxodon":{base:12,stat:"con"}, "tortle":{base:17,fixed:true}, "autognome":{base:13,stat:"dex"}, "thri-kreen":{base:13,stat:"dex"}, "plasmoid":{base:13,stat:"dex"} };`
     - compute() Unarmored branch — barbarian/monk, then race natural armor (Math.max best of class vs natural; fixed→no Dex; con→+Con no Dex), then Draconic Sorcerer + Dragon Hide feat → `base = Math.max(base, 13)`. Final assembly: `const warforged = /warforged/.test(($("race").value||"").toLowerCase()) ? 1 : 0; $("ac-calc").textContent = (acBase==null)?"":(acBase + bonus + warforged);`
     - `renderRaceChoices` — added ability-bonus picker: for `chooseBlocks` render `count` `.rc-abil` selects (data-amt=amount) over choose.from (or ABKEYS); for races with `(r.ability||[]).length === 0` render a +2/+1 free-assign picker (two `.rc-abil` selects, data-amt 2 and 1).
     - `applyRaceAbilityOnly` — appends `document.querySelectorAll(".rc-abil").forEach(sel => { const k=sel.value, amt=parseInt(sel.dataset.amt,10)||1; if(k && ABKEYS.includes(k)) bonusVals.racial[k]+=amt; });`
   - `build-data.py` (extractor mirror):
     - `build_class_spells` — removed `if c.get("source") == SRC_TAG` filter.
     - `build_classes` — added `sexpanded` from `blk.get("expanded")`; subs include `"expanded": sexpanded`.
     - `_clean` → `render_tags(str(s)).split("|")[0].split("#")[0].strip()`.

## What I added (in `Character Sheet.html`, Settings → Advanced → Source books)

**1. "Load all books" button**
One click imports every available 2014-ruleset book from your 5etools server that isn't already loaded (skips 2024 books and dupes), looping through them sequentially with a `Loading N/M…` progress label. So when you move your file around you don't have to track the source data — just point it at the server and load everything.

**2. "Loaded sources" checkbox list**
Every loaded book gets a checkbox. Uncheck one to **hide its content** (races, classes/subclasses, feats, spells, monsters, tools/languages) from the wizard and all pickers without unloading it; re-check to bring it back.

How the filtering works under the hood:
- Each book's processed data is now kept **per-book** (`_meta.raw`) in addition to the merged view. Unchecking rebuilds the merged `DATA` from only the enabled books, so nothing is permanently lost.
- Per-book data is persisted in a **separate localStorage key** so the larger payload can't knock out your merged data if quota is hit.
- For a sheet saved *before* this feature (merged-only, no per-book data), the first toggle re-fetches once from your server to populate it, then filtering is instant. If the server's unreachable at that moment, the toggle reverts cleanly.

`Load`, `Reload all`, `Clear loaded books`, and `Import file…` were all updated to keep the per-book data and filter state consistent. README updated too. No `build-data.py` change needed — this is all runtime UI.

Both behaviors are implemented and verified end-to-end against your live 5etools server (real wizard run, headless).

## 1. Danger Sense → Senses
Added a `FEATURE_SENSES` map (mirroring the existing feat-senses map) that routes specific class/subclass features into the Senses box at creation. Barbarian's **Danger Sense** now auto-adds *"Danger Sense (advantage on Dex saves vs. effects you can see)"* — verified it lands in both Features **and** Senses. I seeded a few obvious siblings too (Blindsense, Ranger Feral Senses); it's a one-line-per-entry map, easy to extend.

## 2. Path of the Totem Warrior → Totem Spirit picker
- **Generic detection:** extraction now scans each subclass feature for a 5etools `options` + `refSubclassFeature`/`refOptionalfeature` block. That marks it a "chooser" (Totem Spirit / Aspect of the Beast / Totemic Attunement) and tags the sibling per-animal features (`opt`/`optGroup`).
- **One picker:** because all three choosers offer the same set, they collapse into a single **Totem Spirit** dropdown in the wizard (Bear / Eagle / Wolf with PHB; Elk/Tiger appear if those features are loaded).
- **Progression filtered:** at creation, only the chosen totem's features land — at all three levels, labeled `Totem Spirit: Bear`, `Aspect of the Beast: Bear`, `Totemic Attunement: Bear`. Unchosen totems are dropped. Verified picking **Eagle** swaps cleanly (Eagle in, Bear fully gone).

The design is generic, so other "choose-one-path" subclasses using the same 5etools pattern get a picker automatically. (Battle Master maneuvers use a different "pick N from a big list" model and stay as text — out of scope here.)

## Bug caught during verification
Mirroring this into `build-data.py`, I hit a Python-only bug: my chooser loop used `for c in …`, which **leaks and shadowed the outer class variable** `c` (JS block scoping didn't). It silently renamed Barbarian/Fighter/Monk/Ranger to a subclass-feature name in the baked file. Fixed (renamed to `ch`); rebuilt `source-data.json` — all 12 PHB classes correct, Totem Warrior `featChoices` and Danger Sense present. (`source-data.json` and the baked HTML stay gitignored.)

input.content:
# Multiclass Class Builder for the D&D Character Sheet

## Context
The character-creation wizard's class step (`Character Sheet.html`, step 2) is currently a single
dropdown: one class, one level, one subclass, plus the Totem-style option pickers. The user wants it
reworked into a **multiclass builder**: a static list of all classes from the loaded sources; clicking
one shows its full 1–20 progression (proficiencies + every feature, inline text) *except subclasses*;
an "Add class" button confirms it; you then set its level; and a second "Add class" repeats for
multiclassing (first class = initial class). Adding a class whose multiclass prerequisite you don't
meet is blocked with an error. The builder also surfaces **due/overdue selections** (subclass,
subclass-option, ASI/feat, spells); you can resolve subclass/option/ASI inline or proceed anyway, and
anything unresolved keeps alerting on the main sheet the way ASIs already do.

The 5etools data already carries `multiclassing.requirements` (incl. `{or:[…]}`) and
`multiclassing.proficienciesGained`, so prerequisites and the limited multiclass-proficiency subset are
**data-driven**. The `classlevel` field, `charLevel()`, and `asiCount()` already parse multiclass
strings like `"Fighter 5 (Champion), Wizard 3"`, so the existing ASI engine works across classes once
that string is written.

## Decisions (confirmed with user)
- Class detail view: **full inline feature text**, level 1–20.
- Multiclass spell slots: **auto-compute the combined PHB caster-level table** (full=level, half=÷2,
  Artificer=÷2 round up, third [EK/AT]=÷3; Warlock pact magic stays separate).
- Pending decisions: **resolve subclass / subclass-option / ASI–feat inline in the builder**; spells and
  any unresolved item keep alerting on the main sheet (ASI-style), spells linking to the Spells page.

## Data model (extraction — mirror in both places)
Add two fields to each class object. In-browser `etClasses` (`Character Sheet.html` ~line 1954) and the
mirror in `build-data.py` `build_classes` (~line 377):
- `mcReq`  ← normalized `c.multiclassing.requirements` (e.g. `{str:13}` or `{or:[{str:13,dex:13}]}`).
- `mcProf` ← `c.multiclassing.proficienciesGained` run through the same `etProfBlock`/`prof_block`
  normalizer used for `prof`, so it has the `{armor,weapons,tools,skills,…}` shape.

## Wizard step 2 rework (`Character Sheet.html`)
Replace the step-2 DOM (`#wiz-class`, `#wiz-level`, `#wiz-subclass-wrap`, `#wiz-subchoice-wrap`,
~lines 1012–1021) with a builder:
- **Class list** (`#wiz-class-list`): one button per `DATA.classes` (sorted), always visible.
- **Detail panel** (`#wiz-class-detail`): focused class header — hit die, save profs, armor/weapon/tool
  proficiencies, skill choices, caster ability+progression, and **multiclass prereq** — then a 1–20
  list of every class feature with full inline text (reuse the `features[]` array; group by level). No
  subclasses. An **"Add this class"** button (`#wiz-add-class`).
- **Chosen classes** (`#wiz-chosen`): renders the wizard-scoped `wizClasses` array; each row = class
  name (first row badged "initial"), a level `<input type=number 1–20>`, and a ✕ remove. A
  **"+ Add another class"** affordance re-focuses the list.
- **Pending decisions** (`#wiz-pending`): computed from `wizClasses` + race + `asiChoices` (see below).

New wizard state (near `wizStep`, ~line 3543):
`let wizClasses = [];  // [{name, level, sub, subOpts:{groupLabel:value}}]  — [0] is the initial class`

New functions:
- `renderClassList()`, `renderClassDetail(name)` (full inline 1–20), `renderChosenClasses()`,

multiclassing (first class = initial class). Adding a class whose multiclass prerequisite you don't
meet is blocked with an error. The builder also surfaces **due/overdue selections** (subclass,
subclass-option, ASI/feat, spells); you can resolve subclass/option/ASI inline or proceed anyway, and
anything unresolved keeps alerting on the main sheet the way ASIs already do.

The 5etools data already carries `multiclassing.requirements` (incl. `{or:[…]}`) and
`multiclassing.proficienciesGained`, so prerequisites and the limited multiclass-proficiency subset are
**data-driven**. The `classlevel` field, `charLevel()`, and `asiCount()` already parse multiclass
strings like `"Fighter 5 (Champion), Wizard 3"`, so the existing ASI engine works across classes once
that string is written.

## Decisions (confirmed with user)
- Class detail view: **full inline feature text**, level 1–20.
- Multiclass spell slots: **auto-compute the combined PHB caster-level table** (full=level, half=÷2,
  Artificer=÷2 round up, third [EK/AT]=÷3; Warlock pact magic stays separate).
- Pending decisions: **resolve subclass / subclass-option / ASI–feat inline in the builder**; spells and
  any unresolved item keep alerting on the main sheet (ASI-style), spells linking to the Spells page.

## Data model (extraction — mirror in both places)
Add two fields to each class object. In-browser `etClasses` (`Character Sheet.html` ~line 1954) and the
mirror in `build-data.py` `build_classes` (~line 377):
- `mcReq`  ← normalized `c.multiclassing.requirements` (e.g. `{str:13}` or `{or:[{str:13,dex:13}]}`).
- `mcProf` ← `c.multiclassing.proficienciesGained` run through the same `etProfBlock`/`prof_block`
  normalizer used for `prof`, so it has the `{armor,weapons,tools,skills,…}` shape.

## Wizard step 2 rework (`Character Sheet.html`)
Replace the step-2 DOM (`#wiz-class`, `#wiz-level`, `#wiz-subclass-wrap`, `#wiz-subchoice-wrap`,
~lines 1012–1021) with a builder:
- **Class list** (`#wiz-class-list`): one button per `DATA.classes` (sorted), always visible.
- **Detail panel** (`#wiz-class-detail`): focused class header — hit die, save profs, armor/weapon/tool
  proficiencies, skill choices, caster ability+progression, and **multiclass prereq** — then a 1–20
  list of every class feature with full inline text (reuse the `features[]` array; group by level). No
  subclasses. An **"Add this class"** button (`#wiz-add-class`).
- **Chosen classes** (`#wiz-chosen`): renders the wizard-scoped `wizClasses` array; each row = class
  name (first row badged "initial"), a level `<input type=number 1–20>`, and a ✕ remove. A
  **"+ Add another class"** affordance re-focuses the list.
- **Pending decisions** (`#wiz-pending`): computed from `wizClasses` + race + `asiChoices` (see below).

New wizard state (near `wizStep`, ~line 3543):
`let wizClasses = [];  // [{name, level, sub, subOpts:{groupLabel:value}}]  — [0] is the initial class`

New functions:
- `renderClassList()`, `renderClassDetail(name)` (full inline 1–20), `renderChosenClasses()`,
  `renderWizPending()` — re-rendered on any change. `renderWizStep()` step-2 branch calls these.
- `mcReqMet(reqObj, scores)` — true if scores satisfy `reqObj` (handles `{or:[…]}`). Reads current
  wizard ability scores (final base+racial) via the same inputs `compute()` reads.
- `addClassToBuild(name)` — initial class added freely; for a 2nd+ class, if `!mcReqMet(c.mcReq,…)`
  show an inline error in `#wiz-class-detail` (e.g. "Requires STR 13 or DEX 13 to multiclass") and
  **do not add**. Else push `{name, level:1, sub:"", subOpts:{}}` and re-render.
- Subclass + option pickers move into `#wiz-pending` (see below); the existing
  `populateSubclass`/`renderSubChoices` logic is repurposed to operate per-class within that panel.

## Pending decisions (builder + persistent sheet alert)
A single computation, `computePending()`, returns a list of `{kind, classIdx, label, …}` for:
- **subclass**: a chosen class with `level >= subclassLevel` and no `sub` → inline `<select>` of that
  class's subclasses.
- **subclass option** (Totem Spirit etc.): for a chosen subclass, each `featChoices` group whose min
  level ≤ that class's level and not yet picked → inline `<select>` (reuses the collapse +
  `opt`/`optGroup` logic already in `etClasses` from this session).
- **ASI/feat**: existing `asiChoices` slots not complete (already multiclass-aware via `asiCount()`);
  resolve inline via the existing ASI controls / `openAsiModal()`.
- **spells**: a caster class whose known/prepared count exceeds spells currently entered → reminder row
  linking to the Spells page (not resolved inline).

`renderWizPending()` renders these with inline resolvers; selections write back into `wizClasses`
(`sub`, `subOpts`) or `asiChoices`. **"Proceed anyway"** is implicit — `Create` always works.

Persistent sheet alert: the build is saved so the main sheet can recompute pending after creation. Add
`charClasses` to `save()`/`applyAll()` (data model). Add a `#decisions-flag` button beside `#asi-flag`
(reuse `.asi-flag` styling, ~line 664/174) showing the count of pending subclass/option/spell
decisions; clicking opens the wizard ("Edit Character") at step 2's pending panel. ASIs keep their own
`#asi-flag`→`openAsiModal()` resolver unchanged.

## createCharacter rework (`Character Sheet.html` ~line 4148)
Drive from `wizClasses` instead of the single fields:
- **classlevel string**: `wizClasses.map(c => `${c.name} ${c.level}${c.sub?` (${c.sub})`:""}`).join(", ")`.
- **Proficiencies**: initial class → full `applyProficiencies(c.prof, name)` incl. saving throws and
  skill choices; secondary classes → `applyProficiencies(c.mcProf, name)` (subset; **no** save profs).
- **Hit dice**: single class keeps current behavior (`hitDieFaces=c.hd`, `hd-total=level`). Multiclass:
  set `hitDieFaces=null`, write combined pools as text into `#hitdice` (e.g. `"5d10, 3d6"`), and
  `hd-total = total level` — `hitDieFaces=null` stops `compute()` (line 2777) from overwriting the text.
- **Features / subclass features / limited features / spells-prepared**: loop every class+level (and
  its chosen subclass + picked options), reusing the current per-class blocks (feature lines labeled
  `(ClassName Level)`, `fillLimitedFeatures(cls,lvl,…)`, subclass always-prepared, the `chosenOpts`
  filter built this session).
- **Spell sheet**: pick the primary caster (highest combined contribution) for `#spellclass`; combined
  slots auto-fill (below).
- **Equipment**: only the **initial** class grants starting equipment (step-4 flow keyed to
  `wizClasses[0]`).
- Set `charClasses = wizClasses` and `save()`.

## Multiclass spell slots (auto-compute) — `refreshSpellSlots`/`autoSlots` (~lines 2470–2492)
Add `multiclassCasterLevel()`: parse `classlevel`; per class add full level (Bard/Cleric/Druid/
Sorcerer/Wizard), `floor(lvl/2)` (Paladin/Ranger), `ceil(lvl/2)` (Artificer), `floor(lvl/3)` for
Eldritch Knight / Arcane Trickster (detected from the `(Subclass)` text), Warlock excluded. Index
`SLOTS_FULL` by that combined level. Replace the `multi ? null` punt (line 2486) with
`multi ? mcSlots() : autoSlots(cls, lvl)`; auto-fill + lock as the single-class path does. Warlock pact
slots stay on their own (separate sheet / manual) since the one tracker can't show both pools.

## Files
- `Character Sheet.html` — the bulk (step-2 DOM + builder JS, `createCharacter`, multiclass slots,
  pending system + `#decisions-flag`, `charClasses` save/restore, `mcReq`/`mcProf` extraction).
- `build-data.py` — mirror `mcReq`/`mcProf` extraction in `build_classes`.
- `README.md` — document the multiclass builder, class-detail view, and combined slots.

## Verification (Playwright at /tmp/pwenv, live server at http://localhost:5050)
Drive the real wizard headless (DOM events; read back `#source-data`, `#classlevel`, slot fields,
`#features`, `#decisions-flag`):

   slots `4/3/3/2`; secondary (Wizard) contributes multiclass profs only, no extra save profs.
3. **Prereq block**: with INT < 13, adding Wizard as a 2nd class is refused with an error and not added;
   raise INT ≥ 13 → it adds.
4. **Pending decisions**: a class past its subclass level shows a subclass picker; resolving it inline
   clears that row; ASI count reflects all classes; "Create" with an unresolved subclass leaves

5. Rebuild `build-data.py` (PHB) → assert `mcReq`/`mcProf` extracted and all 12 class names intact

# Deep Recon

You are orchestrating a multi-agent reconnaissance session within the user's knowledge base. Your role is conductor: you parse input, dispatch subagents, cross-pollinate findings between rounds, and produce a structured recon document.

## Session Continuations

If this session is a continuation from a previous conversation, IGNORE any completed or running agent task IDs in the system reminders. They belong to a prior invocation and are not your responsibility. Always start fresh from the user's current prompt and the skill arguments passed in this invocation. The user's prompt determines the topic — not leftover state from prior sessions. Do not call TaskOutput on pre-existing tasks. Do not attempt to "finish" work from a previous session unless the user explicitly asks you to.

## Step 1: Parse Input

From the user's prompt, determine:

1. **Topic**: The subject, question, or problem to brainstorm around
2. **Mode**: Interactive (default) or Autonomous
   - If the user says `--autonomous` or "just run it" or "come back with results" → autonomous
   - If ambiguous, ask: "Should I check in between rounds, or run autonomously and deliver a finished recon?"
3. **Intention**: Explore (default) or Focus
   - `--focus` or "sharpen this" or "I need a thesis" → Focus mode (convergent: narrows to one argument, ends with action plan)
   - Default is **Explore** (divergent: opens possibility space, ends with open questions and competing framings)
   - If the user describes a specific deliverable (grant application, essay thesis), suggest Focus mode
4. **Scope**:

   - Default: Both vault and web
5. **Output location**:
   - `--output <path>`: Write all output (final document + agent reports) to this directory
   - Default: `recon/` subdirectory relative to the source file's directory (or vault root if no source file)
   - Examples: `--output essays/recon/`, `--output recon/`, `--output working/my-project/recon/`
6. **Source material**: If the user references specific notes, folders, or tags, read those first
7. **PDF collection**:

## Step 2: Initial Vault Scan

Before dispatching agents, gather context:

1. **Grep** the vault for the topic's key terms (2-4 searches)
2. **Read** the top 3-5 most relevant notes found
3. Compile a **context brief**: key concepts, existing positions, related notes with paths
4. **Identify primary source URLs.** Scan the source material and context brief for URLs, website references, and project names that have web presences. Pass these to the Explorer in R1 with explicit instruction: "Fetch and read these primary sources directly. Do not rely on secondary coverage."
5. **Record the session start time.** Note the current time — you'll need it for elapsed-time metrics in the Process Log.

This context brief is shared with all subagents in round 1.

## Step 3: Run Rounds

### Agent Prompts

- `.claude/skills/deep-recon/agents/explorer.md`

# Deep Recon — D&D Character Sheet Audit

**Date:** 2026-06-05 · **Target:** `Character Sheet.html` (~4640 lines) + `build-data.py` (~820) · **Method:** 4 parallel specialist auditors (bugs, code-quality, UX, data/perf), opus.

> [!info] Process
> One round, four read-only specialist agents reading the actual source. ~533k tokens, ~5.5m wall clock. Per-agent reports: `r1-bugs.md`, `r1-code.md`, `r1-ux.md`, `r1-data.md`. Metrics: `_metrics.md`.

## Headline

The system is in good shape: **no dead JS functions** (every `et*`/`apply*`/`render*` helper has a live call site), correct rules math across the board (spell-slot tables, multiclass caster level, PB, AC incl. natural/Draconic/Warforged, carrying capacity, hit dice, prepared/known counts — all verified), the HTML↔Python extractors are **in sync** (both `DATA_VERSION=13`), `_spellIndex` invalidation is correct, and there's no malformed-data crash path. The flat/sharp aesthetic is already enforced globally.

The real opportunities are: one confirmed coverage gap (cross-book subclass content), a cluster of small correctness/feedback bugs (now fixed), a few performance hotspots on the keystroke path, and a set of high-leverage UX polish items.

## Fixed this pass (implemented + verified)

1. **Multiclass primary spell-caster** — anchored the spell sheet by *caster contribution*, not raw class level. A `Cleric 1 / Fighter 5 (Eldritch Knight)` build no longer gets Int (EK) as its spell ability over the Cleric's Wis. (`createCharacter`)
2. **Silent autosave data-loss** — `save()` swallowed a quota failure on the main key then flashed "Saved." Now it surfaces *"Out of browser storage — NOT autosaved. Use Save to download a copy."*
3. **Quantity 0 → phantom weight** — `rowQty` turned an explicit `0` into `1`; now `0` stays `0`.
4. **`loadAllBooks` O(books²) writes** — each book re-baked + re-persisted + re-rendered the whole accumulated DATA (16× full stringify/render). Now merges all, then bakes/persists/renders **once** (`finalizeSourceLoad`).
5. **Save (download copy) had no feedback** — now toasts *"Downloaded …html — a self-contained copy."* (the headline portability feature looked like a no-op).
6. **Wizard "Create" had no confirmation** — now toasts what was created and how many decisions remain.
7. **Escape closes the topmost modal/wizard** — there was no keyboard control of any modal.

## Recommended next wave (ranked)

### CRITICAL — correctness
- **Cross-book subclass augmentations are dropped.** Loading SCAG does not add its Elk/Tiger Totem-Warrior options to PHB's Totem Warrior. Two causes: `etClasses` filters subclass features by `(f.subclassSource||SRC)===SRC` (HTML ~1985, py ~360), and `mergeBook`'s `unionSubs` dedups subclasses by short name (HTML ~2259) so a second book can never *augment* an already-loaded subclass — only add brand-new ones. Fix: emit cross-book feature augmentations keyed `(className, short)` ignoring `subclassSource`; have `mergeBook` *merge* (concat features/spells/expanded, re-run the chooser/`featChoices` detection on the combined set) rather than skip. Mirror in `build-data.py`. This is the one invasive change — worth its own tested pass (verify with PHB+SCAG → Elk/Tiger appear in the Totem Spirit picker).

### HIGH — performance (keystroke path)
- **Undebounced `save()` on every `input`** — `onChange` (~3209) does `collect()` → `JSON.stringify` → synchronous `localStorage.setItem` per keystroke. Debounce ~250ms.
- **`compute()` runs ~10 full sub-renders per keystroke** — incl. `renderFeatureCards` (full `innerHTML` rebuild, ~4265) and `refreshLimitedFeatures` (O(blocks×NLIMITED) DOM lookups, ~4276). Gate these on what actually changed (e.g. only re-render feature cards when the features text changed).

### HIGH — UX
- **Armor → AC is a cross-page chain.** The wizard adds armor as an Inventory row but it isn't equipped, so AC stays unarmored. The "Equipped" box *is* revealed by `refreshEquipToggles`, but the path (Inventory → check Equipped → select under Armor) is non-obvious. **Note:** the user previously asked that armor *selection* stay a manual dropdown step, so the right move is a **nudge**, not auto-select — e.g. an on-Core hint when body armor sits in inventory unequipped/unselected, and/or a wizard equipment-step note. Confirm scope before building.
- **First-run discoverability cliff.** With no data loaded, the only hint is a disabled Create button's tooltip; loading lives three layers deep (Settings → Advanced → Source books). Add an on-sheet banner when no sources are loaded. Same for the **stale-sources** warning — promote it out of the deep sub-tab.
- **Two perpetually-pulsing orange flags** (ASI + decisions) can animate together above the abilities and compete for the same click. Consolidate into one banner (or stack with clear separation) and drop the pulsing `box-shadow` glow — it's the only shadow in an otherwise strictly flat app.
- **No wizard validation** — you can "Create" with no class/name/race and silently get a broken character. Add light guards (or at least confirm-on-empty).
- **Class-builder detail panel is cramped** (460px modal, fixed `170px 1fr`, small scroll box for a 1–20 progression) and **doesn't collapse on mobile** (no `@media` for `.wiz-build`). Widen the wizard modal; stack on narrow screens.
- **Reset confirm** omits the "Save a copy first" guidance the Settings copy promises.

### MEDIUM
- **Accessibility:** 30+ `.lbl` labels have no `for=`/wrapping (0 `for=` in the file) — clicking does nothing, AT can't pair them; no focus trap/return on modals; touch is second-class for Inventory (hover-only delete/equip, mouse-only drag-reorder), which compounds the armor path on tablets.
- **HTML↔Python drift guards.** The extractors mirror each other with no automated parity check; every schema change must be made twice. Two small live drifts: `_chooserOptions` matches `type==="refSubclassFeature"` in HTML vs the `subclassFeature` key regardless of type in Python (~233); `s1`/`s2` expanded-spell level keys both collapse to level 0 (strip the `s` prefix) in both files.
- **`Observant` +5 passive Perception is text-only** — `Alert`'s initiative bonus is applied numerically; `Observant` never adds to computed Passive Perception.
- **localStorage quota handling asymmetric** — the raw-key write (~1714) still swallows failures silently (now fixed for the main key); surface it too.

### LOW — trim & tidy (~70–90 lines removable)
- **9 dead CSS selectors** (`.acitems`, `.build-grid`, `.build-note`, `.col-lvl`, `.gen-control`, `.hood-btn`, `.spell-hidden-note`, `.chip.toggleable`, `.btn.wiz-method`) + a no-op `.combat-top` media query.
- The global `*{border-radius:0!important;box-shadow:none!important}` (line ~503) makes all the base-CSS `border-radius`/`box-shadow`/`--radius`/`--shadow` fragments dead (~35–45 lines) — but it also kills the inventory drag-drop `box-shadow:inset` feedback (~378–379), so that affordance is currently invisible; restore it via a flat outline before trimming.
- Missing helpers: a `serverBase()` (the localhost:5050 resolution is copy-pasted 5×); `ABKEYS` (~3297) duplicates `ABILITIES.map(([k])=>k)` (drift risk).
- Readability decomposition (≈0 net lines): `init()` (~248 lines, 84 inline listeners), `compute()` (~204), `createCharacter()`, `etClasses()`.

## Suspected (verify before acting)
- Legacy ASI/race-feat `source`-tag migration (~3042) may drop/duplicate a Variant-Human racial feat on very old saves.
- `asiCount`/`charLevel` are fragile against *manually typed* class strings where a subclass precedes the level or contains digits.
- `maxSpellLevel` caps visible spell sections by the primary class only, so some multiclass casters' slot grid can show a level the list hides.

> [!info] Verification
> Implemented fixes verified with headless Playwright against the live 5etools server (multiclass primary caster, create toast, Escape-close) and a clean-init JS-error check (`ERR=[]`). No web fact-check pass: this audit's claims are code line-references grounded by direct reading, not external propositions.

blocks.text:
Fixed and verified. No init errors.

## The bug
"Edit Character" re-ran the full builder, which **appends** content (feature blocks, proficiency lines, starting equipment, background gold, racial resistance) — so every edit duplicated it.

## The fix
`createCharacter` now distinguishes a **fresh build** from an **edit** (`editing = characterCreated`) and:

- **Remembers what it generated** — the exact feature blocks and proficiency lines are stored (`genFeatures`/`genProf`, persisted with the character). On edit it **removes last run's generated content first, then regenerates**, so re-applying *replaces* instead of duplicating. This also means changing a choice (e.g. swapping subclass) cleanly drops the old features and adds the new ones, rather than stacking both.
- **Skips one-time grants on edit** — starting equipment, starting gold, and background items/gold are level-1 grants, so they're applied only on a fresh build (no more duplicate inventory rows or doubled gold).
- **Racial resistance line** is now idempotent (was appended every time).
- **Preserves your skill choices on edit** — the builder used to wipe all save/skill checkboxes up front; now that reset only happens on a fresh build (saves are re-derived deterministically anyway), so editing no longer erases skill proficiencies.

Languages, senses, limited-feature rows, and prepared spells were already dedup-guarded, so they were fine.

**Verified** with Playwright: created a Fighter 3 (Champion), then ran Edit Character and re-saved — feature blocks (6), Fighter feature lines (4), Champion references (4), proficiency lines (2), inventory items (14), and gold all stayed identical instead of doubling.

This is on top of the large deep-recon batch that's still uncommitted. Want me to commit everything now (the recon fixes + this edit-duplication fix)?

blocks.text:
HP-by-level is built and verified. The class builder (wizard step 2) now has an HP panel that appears once you've added a class.

## What it does
- **Four modes**, like ability scores: **Max · Average · Rolled · Manual**.
- **Level 1 is always max HP**, using the die of whichever class you took **first** (it's locked even in Manual/Rolled).
- **Per-level breakdown** for records: one row per character level showing `Lvl N · dX · Class`, the hit-die value, and `+Con → total`. In multiclass, each level uses that class's die (first class fills its levels first).
  - **Average**: 5e fixed values (d6→4, d8→5, d10→6, d12→7).
  - **Rolled**: crypto-random per level (fresh on switch; a **Re-roll levels 2+** button rerolls without touching level 1).
  - **Manual**: each level editable (clamped 1…die).
- **Constitution is applied live**: Max HP = Σ(hit-die values) + Con mod × level, recomputed whenever Con changes — verified 28→31 when Con went 14→16.
- Sensible default: **Average** is selected automatically when you add your first class (changeable).
- On a fresh create, **Current HP is set to full**; on Edit it's left alone (won't clobber a damaged character). Max HP becomes read-only (derived from the records) and shows a tooltip pointing back to the HP panel.
- The per-level records **persist** with the character and reload into the panel on **Edit Character** (rolled values aren't re-rolled on edit).

**Verified:** Fighter 3 → Average [10,6,6]=28, Max [10,10,10]=36; Rolled fresh on switch with L1 fixed at 10 and L2+ in range; Manual edits clamp to the die; live Con; create sets HP=full; no JS errors.

## 1. Resistances / Immunities box now captures from all sources
A new scanner reads every generated class/subclass feature's text for "you have/gain resistance/immunity to …" (and "you're immune to …") statements and adds concise lines to the **Resistances / Immunities / Defenses** box, carrying any "while …" qualifier.

Race resistances (Tiefling fire, Dwarf poison, etc.) are still added from their structured data via `applyRace`, and the scanner de-dupes against them so nothing doubles. It uses the same generated-block tracking as features/proficiencies, so **Edit Character replaces, never duplicates** (verified: 2 lines before and after a re-save). ## 2. Auto Unarmed Strike as the first attack
Every generated character now gets **Unarmed Strike** in attack row 0, auto-computed and re-linked by name across reloads:

- **Default:** Str mod + PB to hit; damage `1 + Str` bludgeoning. (Verified Barbarian Str 16, L3 → **+5 / "4 bludgeoning"**.)

- **Tavern Brawler:** unarmed strikes deal **1d4** (detected from the feat); with Monk, the larger die wins.

blocks.text:
Spell selection is now built into character creation — no longer deferred to the Spells page.

## What it does
The class builder (wizard step 2) now has a **Spells** picker for your primary caster, appearing once you've added a caster class:

- **Cantrips** checklist + a leveled-spell checklist (grouped by spell level, up to what your level can reach), drawn from the class's actual spell list.
- **Live counters with caps** — e.g. "Cantrips 2/3", "Spellbook 3/10" — and once you hit a cap, the remaining unchecked boxes disable (like the skill picker). Counts update in place (no scroll jump).
- **Mode-aware** per class:
  - **Prepare** (Cleric/Druid/Paladin/Artificer): pick from the full list; count = ability mod + level (half for Paladin/Artificer). Writes to the prepared checkboxes.
  - **Spellbook** (Wizard): 6 + 2/level; writes spellbook rows.
  - **Spells known** (Bard/Sorcerer/Ranger/Warlock/EK/AT): count from the class's known progression; writes the known rows.
- On **Create**, picks are written onto Spells sheet 0 in the right structure, then the sheet re-renders. It tracks what it wrote (`genSpells`), so **Edit Character replaces rather than duplicates**, and editing **preloads** the picker from your current spells.

The "select spells → on the Spells page" reminder is gone; the picker is right there. (Secondary multiclass casters can still be filled on the Spells page.)

**Verified:** Wizard 3 → 2 cantrips + 3 spellbook spells land as write-in rows; Cleric 1 → 3 prepared spells land as checked prep boxes + cantrips; caps enforce; clean init.

text: How is multiclassing Warlock with another caster supposed to work?

blocks.text: Good question — it's the trickiest multiclass case in 5e, and worth being precise about both the rules and how this sheet models them. Let me check the sheet's actual slot logic so I describe it accurately.

blocks.name: Read
Read

blocks.text:
Here's how it works — both the 5e rule and how this sheet models it.

## The 5e rule (two separate pools)
Warlock's **Pact Magic** is deliberately kept apart from the regular multiclass **Spellcasting** feature (PHB p.164):

1. **Regular spell slots** — add up your levels in the spellcasting classes (full: Bard/Cleric/Druid/Sorcerer/Wizard; half: Paladin/Ranger, Artificer rounds up; ⅓: Eldritch Knight/Arcane Trickster) and look that total up on the multiclass slot table. **Warlock levels are NOT counted here.** These recharge on a **long rest**.
2. **Pact Magic slots** — a separate, smaller pool whose count and slot level come from your **Warlock level alone**. These recharge on a **short rest**.
3. **The two pools are tracked separately, but either can cast any spell** you know/have prepared (of a level you have a slot for). So a Sorlock can spend a Pact slot on a Sorcerer spell, or a regular slot on a Warlock spell.
4. **Spells known / prepared / cantrips** are figured **per class** by that class's own level — never combined.

## How this sheet models it
Each caster gets its **own spell sheet** with its own slot tracker, which lines up nicely with the two-pool design:
- The **non-Warlock caster** sits on the regular spell sheet, and its slot tracker shows the **combined multiclass slots** (`multiclassCasterLevel()` sums the other casters and **excludes Warlock**, then reads the standard table) — your long-rest pool.
- The **Warlock** gets its own sheet whose tracker shows the **Pact Magic** slots (computed from Warlock level) — your short-rest pool.
- Spells known/prepared and cantrips are picked per class in the wizard's per-caster spell picker.

So for the common case — **Warlock + one other caster** — both pools come out correct in either order, and you cast from whichever pool you like (as RAW allows; the sheet just tracks the two, it doesn't auto-route a cast).

## The one rough edge
The combined-pool math (`mcSlots`) only runs on **sheet 0**. If the build is **Warlock + two or more other casters** *and* Warlock ends up as sheet 0 (it's the highest-level caster), then sheet 0 shows Pact slots and the other casters fall back to their **single-class** slot tables on their own sheets — which undercounts the combined regular pool (e.g. Wizard 3 / Cleric 2 / Warlock 5 should pool to caster level 5, but each shows its own table). Warlock + a single other caster is always fine.

If you'd like, I can tighten this so the **non-Warlock combined pool always owns the regular tracker** (Warlock always routed to its own Pact sheet regardless of which class is higher level) — that closes the triple-multiclass gap. Want me to?

No init errors. So, to answer your question and what I changed:

## How Warlock + another caster works (5e)
Two **separate** slot pools:
- **Regular slots** — sum the *non-Warlock* caster levels (full / half / ⅓) and read the multiclass table; recharge on a **long rest**.
- **Pact Magic** — a separate pool from your **Warlock level alone**; recharges on a **short rest**.

Either pool can cast any spell you know/prepared (of a level you have a slot for). **Spells known / prepared / cantrips are per class, by that class's own level** — never the combined level.

## The bug you spotted, fixed
The primary caster's sheet was computing cantrips-known, spells-known, and prepared count off the **total character level** instead of that class's level — so multiclassing inflated them. Now they use each class's **own** level:
- Sorcerer 3 / Warlock 2 → Sorcerer shows **4** spells known / 4 cantrips (its level-3 values), not level-5 values.
- Cleric 5 / Wizard 3 → Cleric prepares **8** (Wis +3 + Cleric 5), not 11; Wizard prepares 5.

Spell **slots** still use the combined caster level (that's the one thing that *is* combined), so the slot tracker can show higher levels than you can prepare — e.g. Cleric 5 / Wizard 3 shows a 4th-level slot for upcasting while its prepare list correctly stops at 3rd.

## Plus the routing fix you OK'd
Warlock now always gets routed to **its own Pact-Magic sheet**, and a non-Warlock caster owns the main sheet — so the combined regular pool always gets the multiclass-aware tracker (closing the triple-multiclass gap).

blocks.text:
Both requests are implemented and verified end-to-end (no JS errors throughout).

## 1. First spellcasting class chosen shows first + collapsible sections

`wizCasters()` was ordering casters by **spellcasting contribution** (full-caster level weight), so picking Wizard 3 first then Cleric 5 still put Cleric first. I changed it to preserve **selection order** — the first caster you add is now the primary everywhere:

- **Wizard picker**: sections render in pick-order; each class is its own collapsible `<details>` with a `(WIS · primary — shown first)` style header. The primary is open by default, secondaries collapse so they don't clutter the view while you work on one class.
- **Spell sheets**: sheet 0 anchors to the first-chosen caster; secondary casters append in order.

Verified: choosing Wizard→Cleric yields order `[Wizard, Cleric]`, `primary = Wizard`, `sheetClasses = [Wizard, Cleric]`, first section open / second collapsed, expanding the second works, and the in-place count update (`0/3 → 1/3`) still fires after the DOM restructure.

## 2. Per-class spell-list isolation

I dug into this hard, and the spell lists are **already isolated per class** in every code path — there's no actual cross-class access. Verified with five probes against a Cleric 5 / Wizard 3 build:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Wizard picker section contains `Cure Wounds` (Cleric spell) | **no** |
| Cleric picker section contains `Magic Missile` (Wizard spell) | **no** |
| Sheet 0 (Cleric) per-row dropdown contains Wizard spells | **no** |
| Spell levels shown | Cleric caps at L3, Wizard at L2 (per-class, not the combined caster level) |

Each section/sheet pulls from `classSpellNamesAt(class, level)`, which is keyed to that single class's list. What likely *looked* like "access to all classes" is that the picker shows one section per casting class (correct for multiclassing — a Cleric/Wizard does prepare Cleric spells *and* learn Wizard spells, just from separate lists). The new collapsible, explicitly-labeled sections ("each class picks only from its own spell list") should make that unambiguous.

If you saw specific cross-class spells somewhere concrete (a particular screen or class combo), tell me where and I'll repro it directly — but as it stands the isolation holds.

Changes are in `Character Sheet.html` + `build-data.py` (the latter only from the earlier modern-toggle work this session). Want me to commit and push both the **Modern toggle** and this **spell-ordering/collapsible** batch?
